On Sunday, Tom and Lily went to the park with Mom and Dad. They saw a big slide, a swing, and a sandbox. Tom and Lily wanted to play on the slide, but there was a boy who did not let them. He said, "This is my slide. Go away!"

Tom and Lily felt sad and angry. They went to Mom and Dad and told them what the boy said. Mom and Dad said, "That is very rude. He should share the slide with others. Let's go and talk to him."

Mom and Dad walked to the slide and saw the boy. They said, "Hello, we are Tom and Lily's parents. We want to ask you why you are not letting them play on the slide. The slide is for everyone to enjoy. Can you please share it with them?"

The boy looked at Mom and Dad and said, "No, I don't want to. This is my slide. I came here first. You go away!"

Mom and Dad said, "That is not nice. You are being selfish and mean. You should not talk like that to us or to Tom and Lily. They are your friends. How would you feel if someone did that to you?"

The boy thought for a moment and said, "I would feel bad. I'm sorry. I was wrong. I will share the slide with Tom and Lily. Can we play together?"

Mom and Dad said, "That is very good. We are glad you changed your mind. Yes, you can play together. But remember to be kind and respectful to others. That is how you make friends."

Tom and Lily smiled and said, "Thank you. We forgive you. Let's have fun on the slide."

The boy said, "Okay. Thank you. I'm sorry. Let's have fun."

They all climbed up the slide and slid down one by one. They laughed and cheered. They had a good time on Sunday.

One night, a little girl named Lily could not sleep. She heard a loud sound outside her window. She was scared and ran to her mom and dad's room.

"Mom, Dad, what is that noise?" she asked.

They hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. It's just an owl. An owl is a bird that stays awake at night and makes a hoo-hoo sound."

"Can I see the owl?" Lily asked.

"Sure, let's go to the window and look," her dad said.

They went to the window and saw a big owl sitting on a branch. It had brown feathers, a round face, and big yellow eyes. It looked at them and said, "Hoo-hoo!"

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Lily said.

"Yes, it is," her mom said. "But you know what? The owl is also very calm. It doesn't get scared or angry easily. It just watches and listens to everything around it."

"Really?" Lily asked.

"Yes, really," her dad said. "That's why we recommend you to be like the owl sometimes. When you feel scared or upset, you can try to be calm and think of something that makes you happy. Then you will feel better."

"I see," Lily said. "I want to be like the owl. Can I say hello to the owl?"

"Of course you can," her mom said. "But be quiet, so you don't scare it away."

Lily smiled and whispered, "Hello, owl. You are very calm and nice. I want to be your friend."

The owl blinked and said, "Hoo-hoo!" It seemed to like Lily too.

Lily felt happy and sleepy. She said good night to the owl and her parents. They tucked her in and kissed her. She closed her eyes and dreamed of the owl. She was not scared anymore. She was calm and peaceful.

"Whale, what happened to your eye?" Mia asked.

The whale made a sad noise. It pointed to a big boat in the distance. The boat had a big net and a big hook. The whale said that the boat tried to catch it. The whale fought back and escaped. But the hook hurt its eye.

"That's not nice!" Ben said. "The boat is mean. We don't like the boat."

His mommy came to his room with a glass of water and a spoon. She said, "Tommy, you have to take your medicine. It will make you feel better." She gave him a spoonful of the medicine. It was bitter and Tommy made a face. He did not like the medicine.

He said, "Mommy, I don't want the medicine. It is yucky. Can I have some juice instead?" His mommy shook her head. She said, "No, Tommy, you need the medicine. Juice is too sweet. It will make your throat hurt more. Drink some water. It will help you swallow the medicine."

She gave him the glass of water. Tommy drank some water. He still did not like the medicine. He said, "Mommy, can I have a hug?" His mommy smiled. She said, "Of course, Tommy. I love you very much." She hugged him and kissed his forehead. She said, "You are very brave, Tommy. I am proud of you."

She tucked him in his bed. She gave him his favorite pillow. It was soft and fluffy. It had a picture of a dinosaur on it. Tommy liked dinosaurs. He said, "Mommy, can you tell me a story?" His mommy nodded. She said, "Sure, Tommy. What kind of story do you want to hear?" Tommy said, "A story about dinosaurs. They are big and strong and cool."

His mommy began to tell him a story about dinosaurs. She said, "Once upon a time, there was a little dinosaur named Rex. He was a T-rex, the king of the dinosaurs. He had sharp teeth and claws and a loud roar. He liked to hunt and eat other dinosaurs. He was very hungry and he was looking for food. He saw a big dinosaur with a long neck and a long tail. It was a brontosaurus. It was eating leaves from a tall tree. Rex thought, 'That looks like a tasty snack. I will catch it and eat it.' He ran towards the brontosaurus. He opened his mouth and roared."

Tommy listened to the story. He liked the story. He imagined he was Rex. He roared too. He said, "Rrrrrrr!" His mommy laughed. She said, "You sound like a real T-rex, Tommy. But be careful, the brontosaurus is not afraid of you. It has a secret weapon. Do you know what it is?" Tommy shook his head. He said, "No, Mommy. What is it?" His mommy said, "It is its tail. It can swing its tail like a whip. It can hit you with its tail and make you fall down. It can hurt you very much. You have to be smart and fast to catch it."

She continued the story. She said, "Rex did not know about the brontosaurus's tail. He was too hungry and too angry. He ran faster and faster. He was almost near the brontosaurus. He was ready to bite it. But the brontosaurus saw him. It swung its tail like a whip. It hit Rex with its tail. It hit him hard. It hit him on his nose. Rex felt a big pain. He cried out. He said, 'Ow! Ow! Ow!' He dropped his pillow. He rubbed his nose. He said, 'Mommy, that hurt. The brontosaurus is mean. It hit me with its tail.'"

Mom follows them. She lifts them up, one by one, to see a nest on a branch. They see three eggs inside the nest. They are blue and speckled.

"Wow, eggs!" Lily says.

"Shh, be quiet. The eggs are sleeping. The mommy bird will come back soon. She will keep them warm and safe. When they hatch, they will be baby birds. They will be healthy and strong." mom says.

"Can we touch them?" Tom asks.

"No, no. We can't touch them. They are not ours. They belong to the bird family. We can look, but not touch. If we touch them, we might hurt them or scare them. We have to be gentle and respectful." mom says.

"OK, mom. We understand. We are gentle and respectful." Lily and Tom say.

They look at the eggs for a while. Then they hear a loud squawk. They see the mommy bird flying to the nest. She has a worm in her beak.

"Look, she has food for the eggs!" Lily says.

"Shout, shout, go away!" the mommy bird says. She is angry and scared. She thinks Lily and Tom want to take her eggs.

"Sorry, sorry, we are going. We don't want to take your eggs. We just want to see them. They are very beautiful." mom says.

She puts Lily and Tom down. They walk away from the tree. They wave to the bird family.

"Bye, bye, birds. Have a nice day. Thank you for letting us see your nest." Lily and Tom say.

The mommy bird calms down. She covers her eggs with her wings. She sings a soft song.

Spot saw what was happening. He did not like it when his friends fought. He wanted them to be happy and play together. He had an idea. He ran to the wheel and jumped on it. He barked and wagged his tail. He made the wheel spin faster and faster.

Tom and Mia were surprised. They saw Spot on the wheel. They saw how happy he was. They saw how he shared the toy with them. They felt sorry for being mean to each other. They decided to be nice and take turns.

"Sorry, Mia," Tom said. He got off the wheel and gave it to Mia. "You can go now. I had enough."

"Thank you, Tom," Mia said. She smiled and sat on the wheel. She pushed with her feet and made the wheel spin. She laughed and said, "This is fun!"

Tom and Mia learned a lesson. They learned that sharing is good and fighting is bad. They learned that being friends is better than being selfish. They learned that Spot was a good dog and a good teacher. They hugged Spot and thanked him. They played with the wheel and with Spot. They had a lot of fun.

One day, Sam had a new idea. He wanted to mix his cars and make new ones. He took out his cars from the box and put them on the floor. Lila was an adventurous girl. She liked to explore new places and find new things. One day, she saw a big hole in the wall of her room. She wondered what was inside.

She took her finger and put it in the hole. She felt something soft and furry. She smiled and said, "Hello, who are you?"

A squeaky voice answered, "I am a mouse. Who are you?"

"I am Lila. I live here. Do you live in the hole?"

"Yes, I do. It is cozy and warm. Do you want to see?"

Lila nodded. She was curious. She took her finger out of the hole and said, "Can I come in?"

The mouse said, "Yes, you can. But be careful. It is dark and narrow. Follow me."

Lila crawled into the hole. She felt the mouse's tail in front of her. She followed it deeper and deeper. She saw many things in the hole. She saw nuts and seeds, bits of cloth and paper, shiny buttons and beads. She saw a nest made of fluff and feathers. She saw the mouse's family. They were four little mice. They looked at Lila with big eyes.

"Hello, these are my children. They are very shy. You are the first human they see."

Lila smiled and said, "Hello, you are very cute. I am Lila. I am your friend."

The mouse said, "Thank you, Lila. You are very kind. You are our friend too. Do you want to play with us?"

Lila said, "Yes, I do. What do you play?"

The mouse said, "We play hide and seek, we play catch, we play make believe. We have fun."

Lila said, "That sounds fun. Let's play."

They played for a long time. Lila had fun. She forgot about the time. She forgot about the hole. She forgot about her room. She was happy with her new friends. She was an adventurous girl.

Lily liked to sell things. She had a table in front of her house. She put her toys, books, and clothes on the table. She made a sign that said "Lily's Sale". She hoped people would come and buy her things.

One day, a lady came to Lily's table. She looked at Lily's things. She saw a vase. The vase was blue and had flowers on it. It was Lily's mom's vase. Lily did not know that. She thought it was an old vase. She put it on the table.

The lady said, "How much for the vase?"

Lily said, "One dollar."

The lady said, "That's a good price. I'll take it."

She gave Lily a dollar and took the vase.

Lily was happy. She sold the vase.

But then, her mom came out of the house. She saw the lady with the vase. She said, "Hey, that's my vase! Where did you get it?"

The lady said, "I bought it from your daughter. She was selling it on her table."

Lily's mom was shocked. She said, "Lily, why did you sell my vase? That was a gift from your grandma. It was very special."

Lily said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know. I wanted to sell things. I thought it was an old vase."

Lily's mom was sad. She said, "Lily, you can't sell things that are not yours. That's not nice. You have to ask me first. And you have to be careful with things that are special. They are not for selling."

Lily felt bad. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I won't do it again. Can we get the vase back?"

Lily's mom said, "Maybe. Let's ask the lady."

They went to the lady. They said, "Excuse me, lady. Can we have the vase back? It was a mistake. It was not for selling. It was a gift from Lily's grandma. It was very special."

The lady was nosy. She said, "Oh, really? How special? Is it worth a lot of money? Is it an antique? Is it rare?"

Lily's mom said, "No, it's not. It's just special to us. It has sentimental value. Please, can we have it back?"

The lady said, "Hmm, I don't know. I paid a dollar for it. I like it. It's pretty. Why should I give it back?"

Lily's mom said, "Because it's the right thing to do. It was a mistake. Lily didn't know. She's only three. She's learning. Please, be kind. Give us the vase back."

The lady thought for a moment. She said, "Okay, fine. I'll give you the vase back. But you have to give me my dollar back. And you have to teach Lily not to sell things that are not hers. And you have to be more careful with your things. And you have to say thank you."

Lily's mom said, "Okay, okay. Thank you. Here's your dollar. And Lily, say sorry and thank you."

Lily said, "I'm sorry, lady. Thank you, lady."

They took the vase and went back to the house.

Lily's mom said, "Lily, I'm glad we got the vase back. But you have to be more careful. You can't sell things that are not yours. You have to ask me first. And you have to be respectful of things that are special. They are not for selling. They are for keeping."

Lily said, "I understand, mom. I'm sorry. I love you. And I love grandma. And I love the vase."

They hugged and kissed. They put the vase on the shelf. They looked at it and smiled. It was special.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Poppy shouted. She dropped the stick and ran to the house. She found her mom in the kitchen and showed her the red marks on her hand. "Mom, the ants pinched me! It hurts!"

Mom hugged Poppy and took her to the sink. She washed her hand with water and soap and put a band-aid on it. She kissed Poppy's cheek and said, "I'm sorry, Poppy. The ants were scared and they pinched you to protect their home. You should not poke their ant hill. It is not nice."

Rex was a big dog who loved to chew bones. He had many bones in his yard, but he always wanted more. One day, he saw a small cat walking by with a bone in her mouth. Rex ran after the cat and barked, "Give me your bone!"

The cat was scared and ran away, but Rex was faster. He caught up with the cat and tried to take the bone from her. The cat hissed and scratched Rex's nose. Rex yelped and let go of the bone. The cat ran away with the bone and hid under a car.

Rex was troubled. He did not understand why the cat did not want to share the bone. He thought bones were for dogs, not cats. He felt sad and angry. He went back to his yard and looked at his bones. He had so many, but he still wanted the cat's bone.

Then he heard a whimper. He looked around and saw a small dog hiding behind a fence. The small dog was thin and dirty. He had no bone to chew. Rex felt sorry for the small dog. He remembered how the cat had scratched him and how it had hurt. He did not want to hurt the small dog.

He walked over to the fence and said, "Hello, I am Rex. Do you want a bone?"

The small dog looked up and wagged his tail. He said, "Yes, please. I am Max. I have no bone. I am hungry and lonely."

Rex smiled and picked up a bone from his yard. He gave it to Max and said, "Here, you can have this bone. It is big and tasty. You can chew it as long as you want."

Max took the bone and thanked Rex. He said, "You are very kind, Rex. You are a good friend. Can I stay with you?"

Rex nodded and said, "Of course, you can stay with me. We can share my bones and play together. I have many bones, but I only need one friend."

Rex and Max became friends and chewed their bones happily. Rex learned to share and understand. He did not want the cat's bone anymore. He was happy with what he had.

Amy told her mom and dad about the terrible neighbor. Her mom and dad talked to Mr. Fox. They said, "Mr. Fox, you must be a good neighbor and give back Amy's toys." Mr. Fox felt bad and gave back the toys. From that day on, Mr. Fox was a better neighbor and Amy was happy.

One day, a small cat named Kitty was walking in the busy park. She saw her friend, Puppy, playing with a ball. Kitty felt tired and wanted to find a place to rest.

"Kitty, come play with me!" Puppy said. Kitty shook her head and said, "I am too tired, Puppy. Let's find a shelter to rest in." Puppy agreed and they both started to look around.

They saw a big tree with lots of leaves. Kitty suggested, "Let's go under the tree. It will be a good shelter." They went under the tree and took a nice, long nap. When they woke up, they felt happy and ready to play again.

"Sure, smelly cat," said the crane. "Hop on and I will lift you up."

The smelly cat jumped onto the crane, and up they went. The cat saw the whole town from up high. He was very happy. But then, he saw a door with a lock on it.

"Mr. Crane," said the smelly cat, "can you help me open that door?"

"I am sorry, smelly cat," said the crane. "I cannot open locks. But I can take you back down."

The crane lowered the smelly cat back to the ground. The cat went to find someone else to help open the locked door. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little girl named Sue went for a walk in the park. She saw a tree with a big hole in it. Sue looked inside and found a small, sour fruit. She took a bite and made a funny face. "Yuck! This fruit is too sour!" she said.

Then, a friendly spirit came out of the hole. The spirit asked, "Can you guess what makes the fruit sweet?" Sue thought for a moment and said, "No, I don't know. Please tell me."

The spirit smiled and said, "If you share this fruit with someone you love, it will become sweet." So Sue took the fruit home and shared it with her mom. As they ate the fruit together, it became sweet and delicious.

The moral of the story is that sharing with others can turn something sour into something sweet.

Timmy's mom smiled and said, "Of course we can keep it. But we need to make sure to take care of it. We have to wash our hands before we touch it and make sure it has enough leaves to eat." 

Timmy and his mom took care of the caterpillar every day. They watched it grow bigger and bigger. One day, the caterpillar made a cocoon around itself. Her mom looked at the piece and said, "Be careful, Lily. That piece looks like it might rot soon." 

Lily didn't understand what "rot" meant, but she knew it didn't sound good. She decided to keep her new treasure safe in her room, away from anything that could make it rot. 

Days went by and Lily forgot about the piece until one day, she noticed it had turned brown and was starting to crumble. She remembered what her mom had said and knew it was time to let go of her special treasure. 

Lily said goodbye to the piece and threw it away, knowing that it was better to let it go than to keep it and watch it rot away.

As she kept staring at the port, it started to rain. The rain was so thick that Lucy started to get wet. But despite getting wet, she was still fascinated by the port and wanted to keep looking at it. 

After a while, when the rain stopped and the sun came out, Lucy decided it was time to go inside. But she promised herself to come back every day to stare at the port.

"No, I saw it first!" Max said. "It is mine!"

"She wants to take it from me, but I found it!" Max said, pointing at Lily.

The lady looked at the stone and said, "This is not a gem, children. It is a piece of glass. Someone must have thrown it away. It is not good for you to play with. It might cut you or break."

"Really? It is not a gem?" Lily asked.

Ben and Mia were playing in the living room. They had many toys, but they both wanted the same one: a brown iron that made a funny noise when you pressed a button. Ben grabbed the iron first, but Mia pulled it from his hands.

"Mine!" Ben shouted.

"No, mine!" Mia cried.

They both tugged and pulled on the iron, but neither of them would let go. The iron made a loud beep and a hiss, and they both got scared. They dropped the iron on the floor, and it broke into pieces.

"Uh-oh," Ben said.

"Uh-oh," Mia said.

They looked at each other, and then at the broken iron. They felt bad for breaking the toy, and for fighting with each other. They heard their mom coming from the kitchen.

"What's going on here?" Mom asked.

She saw the mess on the floor, and the sad faces of Ben and Mia. She was not happy.

"Did you break the iron?" Mom asked.

Ben and Mia nodded. They were afraid of getting in trouble.

"Why did you do that?" Mom asked.

"We wanted to play with it," Ben said.

"But we both wanted it," Mia said.

"So you fought over it?" Mom asked.

Ben and Mia nodded again. They felt sorry for what they did.

"Listen, kids," Mom said. "I know you like to play with toys, and that's fine. But you have to learn to share, and to take turns. Fighting over things is not nice, and it can lead to accidents, like breaking the iron. Do you understand?"

Ben and Mia nodded. They understood.

"Sharing is caring," Mom said. "When you share, you make your friends happy, and you can have more fun together. When you fight, you make your friends sad, and you can hurt yourself or others. Which one do you think is better?"

"Sharing," Ben and Mia said.

Ben and Mia hugged each other, and said they were sorry. They felt better, and smiled.

"Pass me some coal, Sam," Tom said. "I will make the eyes."

Sam passed him two pieces of coal. Tom pushed them into the snowman's head. They looked like big, black eyes.

"Now, pass me some more coal, Sam," Tom said. "I will make the mouth."

Sam passed him three pieces of coal. Tom arranged them in a curve on the snowman's head. They looked like a smile.

"OK, let's call him..." Tom said, but he did not finish his sentence. He heard a loud noise behind him. He turned around and saw a big, fast train coming towards them.

"Sam, look out!" Tom shouted. "The train is coming! We have to run!"

Her mom was already there, holding the baby in her arms. She looked at Anna with a stern face. She saw the drum on the shelf and the stick on the floor. She knew what had happened. She said to Anna, in a low voice, "You know you are not supposed to make noise when your brother is sleeping. You know he needs silence. Why did you do that?"

Anna felt tears in her eyes. She wanted to say sorry, but she could not find the words. She looked at the drum, which was supposed to be a fun toy, but now seemed like a bad thing. She wished she had never found it. She wished she had listened to her mom. She learned a hard lesson that day.

Mom gives him the money. He puts a stamp on the letter and puts it in a bin.

"Thank you. Your letter will be on its way soon. Have a nice day." the mailman says, smiling.

"Thank you. You too." Mom says, smiling back.

"Bye, Mr. Mailman. Bye, letter. See you soon, Grandma." Lily says, waving.

They leave the post office and go back to the car. Lily feels happy. She mailed her letter to Grandma. She hopes Grandma will write back soon. She hopes Grandma will come to her home soon.

"Mom, can we go to the park now?" Lily says.

"Sure, honey. Let's go to the park and have some fun." Mom says.

They drive to the park and play on the swings, the slide, the seesaw, and the sandbox. Lily has a lot of fun. She laughs and runs and jumps. She makes new friends. She shares her toys. She has a snack. She drinks some water.

But then, Lily feels dizzy. She feels sick. She feels hot. She feels tired. She does not want to play anymore.

"Mom, I don't feel good." Lily says, holding her head.

"Oh, honey. What's wrong?" Mom says, feeling her forehead.

"I feel dizzy. I feel sick. I feel hot. I feel tired." Lily says, lying down on the bench.

"Oh, no. You have a fever. You are sick. We need to go home and rest. Come on, let's go." Mom says, picking her up.

They go to the car and drive home. Lily feels worse. She closes her eyes and falls asleep. Mom carries her to her bed and tucks her in. She gives her some medicine and some water. She kisses her forehead and says, "I love you, Lily. I hope you feel better soon."

Lily opens her eyes and says, "I love you, Mom. Thank you for taking care of me."

Mom smiles and says, "You're welcome, honey. You're my sweet girl. Now, try to sleep. I'll be right here."

Lily closes her eyes and falls asleep. She dreams of Grandma. She dreams of writing. She dreams of home.

"Because it has long legs?" Lily guessed.

"Why can't it fly, mom?" Tim wondered.

"Well, Tim, the ostrich is too heavy to fly. It is the biggest and heaviest bird in the world. It needs a lot of energy to lift itself off the ground, and its wings are not strong enough to do that," mom said.

"Wow, that's amazing, mom. But I think the ostrich is still charming. It has a funny face and a fluffy tail. Can we feed it, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, Lily. Let's go and get some food for the ostrich. Maybe it will like some carrots or lettuce. But be careful, don't get too close to its beak. It might peck you," mom warned.

Tom and Lily learned their lesson. They never went too far into the water again. They played on the beach safely and happily. They thanked Mom for saving them. They knew that Mom was wise and kind. They knew that the tide was not a toy.

"Look, mom, look, dad, a big snake!" he says, pointing to a long green thing in a glass box. "It is so long and shiny. How does it move?"

Mom and dad smile and explain. "The snake has no legs, Sam. It moves by twisting its body. It can also squeeze things very hard with its muscles. Do you know what muscles are?"

Sam nods. "Yes, I have muscles. They help me run and jump and play. The snake has muscles too?"

"Yes, it does. And it has a brain, too. Just like you and me. The brain helps the snake think and feel and remember. Do you know where your brain is?"

Sam touches his head. "Here, in my head. I have a brain. It helps me learn and talk and dream. The snake has a brain in its head too?"

"Yes, it does. But its brain is very small and different from ours. It does not know many things that we know. It does not talk or read or count. It only knows how to hunt and hide and survive. Do you want to see its brain?"

Sam is curious. He wants to see the snake's brain. He nods. "Yes, I want to see it. How can we see it?"

Mom and dad look at each other. They are not sure if they should show him. They think it might be too scary or gross for him. But they also want to encourage his interest in science. They decide to take him to a special room in the zoo, where they have some animal skulls and brains on display. They warn him that it might look strange and different, but it is not alive or dangerous.

They enter the room and see a table with some glass jars and boxes. Inside, there are different animal brains and skulls. They see a cow brain, a bird brain, a fish brain and a snake brain. They are all different sizes and shapes and colors. Sam is amazed. He looks at them with wide eyes.

"Wow, these are brains?" he asks. "They look so weird. They are not like my brain. They are not like the snake's body. They are not long and shiny. They are round and wrinkly. And they are hot. Why are they hot?"

Mom and dad explain. "They are hot because they are preserved in a special liquid. The liquid keeps them from rotting or drying out. It also makes them safe to touch and study. Do you want to touch one?"

Sam is brave. He wants to touch one. He reaches for the snake brain. He feels it with his fingers. It is soft and squishy and wet. He giggles.

"It feels funny. It feels like jelly. Is this how the snake thinks and feels? With jelly?"

Mom and dad laugh. They are proud of Sam. He is smart and curious and adventurous. They hug him and tell him.

"Yes, Sam, this is how the snake thinks and feels. With jelly. But you think and feel with something much more amazing. You think and feel with your brain. Your brain is the most wonderful thing in the world. It helps you see and learn and love. And we love you very much."

Tim was sad. He went to his mom and said, "Mom, I broke the lamp." His mom was not mad. She hugged Tim and said, "It's okay. We can get a new lamp now." Tim was happy, and they went to the store to buy a new lamp.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a black bear named Ben. Ben loved to eat honey. One day, he saw a big tree with a beehive full of honey. Ben wanted to get the honey, but he was scared of the bees.

Ben asked his friend, a small bird named Sally, "How can I get the honey without getting stung by the bees?" Sally thought for a moment and said, "I can help you. I can talk to the bees and ask them to let you have some honey."

Sally flew to the beehive and talked to the bees. The bees agreed to give Ben some honey. Ben was very happy and thanked Sally for her help. Together, they succeeded in getting the honey. Ben and Sally shared the sweet honey and had a great time. From that day on, they became best friends and always helped each other.

Tom saw Max and Lily and wanted to solve the problem. Tom said, "Max, give the ball back to Lily." Max did not listen. Tom tried again, "Max, if you give the ball back, I will give you a treat." Max thought about the treat and gave the ball back to Lily. Tom was happy that he could solve the problem, and Max was happy to get a treat.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with many shiny things hanging from it. They ran to the tree and looked at the things. They were stars, moons, hearts, and flowers made of metal and glass.

"Wow, look at these!" Lily said. "They are so pretty!"

"I wonder what they are for," Ben said. He reached for a star and tried to pull it off the branch. But it was tied with a string and did not come off. Instead, it made a soft sound, like a bell.

Lily heard the sound and smiled. She grabbed a moon and twisted it gently. It made the same sound, but a little different. She twisted it again and again, and the sound changed each time.

"Listen, Ben, they make music!" Lily said. "Maybe they are magic!"

Ben twisted his star too, and heard the music. He liked it very much. He looked at the other things and wondered what they could do. He saw a heart that was red and shiny. He wanted to twist it and see what would happen.

"Can I have that heart, please?" he asked Lily.

Lily looked at the heart and liked it too. She wanted to keep it for herself. She shook her head and said, "No, it is mine. You have a star, I have a heart."

Ben felt sad and angry. He did not think it was fair. He said, "But I saw it first. You have a moon, I have nothing."

Lily did not care. She said, "Too bad. Find something else."

Ben did not want to find something else. He wanted the heart. He tried to grab it from Lily, but she held it tight. They started to pull and tug, and the heart swung back and forth. The string snapped, and the heart flew away. It landed on the ground and broke into pieces.

Lily and Ben stopped fighting and looked at the heart. They felt sorry and ashamed. They had ruined the magic thing. They had hurt each other. They had made a bad wish.

They hugged and said, "I'm sorry. I love you."

They picked up the pieces and put them back on the branch. They hoped the magic would come back. They hoped the music would play again. They hoped the heart would heal.

They made a new wish. A sweet wish. A wish to share and be happy.

He runs to his mom and says, "Mom, my jeep is broken! It won't go! It won't turn! It won't vroom! What can I do?"

His mom hugs him and says, "Don't worry, Tommy. Maybe the jeep needs new batteries. Or maybe it needs some oil. Or maybe it needs some love. Let's go to the garage and see what we can do."

They go to the garage and find some tools and some batteries and some oil. They open the jeep and look inside. They fix the wires and the gears and the lights. They put in new batteries and some oil. They close the jeep and turn it on.

The jeep starts working again. It goes and turns and vrooms. Tommy is happy. He hugs his mom and says, "Thank you, mom! You fixed my jeep! You are the best! I love you!"

His mom smiles and says, "You're welcome, Tommy. I love you too. Now go have fun with your jeep. But be careful and don't go too fast."

Tommy nods and drives his jeep in the yard. He makes noises like vroom vroom. He pretends he is a firefighter or a soldier or a racer. He loves his jeep.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play and learn together. One day, Anna has a loose tooth. She is happy because she knows the tooth fairy will come and give her a coin.

"Look, Ben, my tooth is wiggly!" Anna says, showing her tooth to Ben.

"Wow, that's cool!" Ben says. "Can I touch it?"

"Okay, but be gentle," Anna says.

Ben touches Anna's tooth with his finger. He feels it move a little. He is curious.

"How does the tooth come out?" he asks.

Anna shrugs. "I don't know. Maybe you have to pull it or wait for it to fall out."

Ben thinks for a moment. He has an idea.

"Maybe I can teach you how to make it come out faster," he says.

Anna is interested. "How?" she asks.

Ben smiles. "Follow me," he says.

He leads Anna to the swing set in the playground. He tells her to sit on a swing and hold on tight. He pushes her hard and fast.

"Are you ready?" he asks.

Anna nods. She likes to swing high.

Ben counts to three. Then he says, "Now, open your mouth and say 'ahh'!"

Anna does what Ben says. She opens her mouth and says "ahh". She feels a breeze on her tongue. She also feels something fly out of her mouth.

She looks down and sees her tooth on the ground. She is surprised and happy.

"Ben, you did it! You taught me how to make my tooth come out!" she says.

Ben is proud and happy too. He runs to pick up Anna's tooth and gives it to her.

"Here you go, Anna. Now you can put it under your pillow and wait for the tooth fairy," he says.

Anna hugs Ben and thanks him. They are both happy. They are good friends. They learned something new and cool.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. They run and jump and slide and swing. They are very jolly.

One day, Tom sees a big hill. He wants to climb it. He says to Jen, "Come on, let's go up the hill. It will be fun."

Jen is not sure. She says, "The hill is too high. We might fall. It is not safe."

Tom says, "Don't be scared. We can do it. It will improve our legs. We will be strong and fast."

Jen does not want to make Tom sad. She says, "OK, I will try. But be careful."

They start to climb the hill. They hold hands and help each other. They are halfway up when they hear a loud noise. It is a big dog. It is barking and running towards them. It looks angry.

Tom and Jen are scared. They try to run down the hill. But they are too fast. They lose their balance. They tumble and roll and bump. They hurt their legs and arms and heads. They cry and scream.

The dog catches up with them. It bites Tom's leg. It is very painful. Jen tries to help Tom. She kicks the dog. But the dog is too strong. It bites Jen's leg too. They are both bleeding.

A man hears their cries. He comes to the park. He sees the dog and the children. He shouts at the dog. He scares it away. He calls for help. He says, "Don't worry, I will help you. You will be OK."

But Tom and Jen are not OK. They have to go to the hospital. They have to get stitches and bandages. They have to stay in bed for a long time. They cannot play in the park anymore. They are not jolly. They are sad. They wish they had not climbed the hill. They wish they had listened to Jen. They learned a hard lesson. The end.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They also liked to look for shiny things in the grass. Sometimes they found coins that people dropped. They put them in a jar at home.

One day, Tom found a big coin that was very shiny. He showed it to Lily and said, "Look, this is a special coin. It has a star on it. I want to keep it."

Lily said, "Wow, that is a nice coin. Can I see it?"

Tom gave her the coin and she looked at it. She said, "It is very pretty. Can I have it?"

Tom said, "No, it is mine. I found it. Give it back."

Lily said, "Please, can I have it? I like it too."

Tom said, "No, no, no. It is mine. Give it back now."

They started to pull the coin from each other. They did not see the dog that was running towards them. The dog saw the shiny coin and wanted to play with it. He jumped and snatched the coin from their hands. He ran away with it.

Tom and Lily were very sad. They cried and shouted, "Come back, dog. Give us our coin. We want our coin."

But the dog did not listen. He ran to the other side of the park and buried the coin in the dirt. He wagged his tail and barked.

Tom and Lily missed their coin. They were very nervous. They did not know what to do. They looked for the dog, but they could not find him. They looked for the coin, but they could not find it. They felt very bad.

They went back to the slide and sat down. They did not want to play anymore. They were quiet and sad.

Then, a man came to them. He was the owner of the dog. He said, "Hello, kids. I'm sorry about my dog. He likes shiny things. He took your coin, didn't he?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, he did. He ran away with it. We don't know where he went. We miss our coin. It was a special coin. It had a star on it."

The man said, "I know where he went. He buried it in the dirt. He does that all the time. Come with me. I'll help you find it."

Tom and Lily followed the man. He took them to the spot where the dog had dug a hole. He said, "Here it is. He hid it here. Do you see it?"

Tom and Lily looked in the hole. They saw the shiny coin. They were very happy. They said, "There it is. There is our coin. Thank you, thank you, thank you."

The man said, "You're welcome, kids. I'm glad you found it. It is a special coin. It has a star on it. You can keep it. But be careful. Don't let my dog see it again. He might take it again."

Tom and Lily said, "OK, we will. Thank you, again. You are very nice."

They took the coin and put it in their pocket. They hugged the man and the dog. They said, "Bye, bye. Have a good day."

They went back to the slide and played. They were happy and smiling. They did not miss their coin anymore. They had it with them. It was a special coin. It had a star on it.

One day, he finds a tie in his dad's closet. He thinks it is a long, colorful snake. He wants to test it. He takes it out and wraps it around his neck. He feels funny. He tries to pull it off, but it is too tight. He starts to cry.

Mom hears him and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the tie around his neck and quickly unties it. She hugs him and tells him he is okay. Mom smiles and kisses him. She tells him she loves him. She tells him she is glad he is curious, but he should also be organized. She tells him he should keep his things in his own place, and not make a mess. She tells him he should ask before he touches other people's things.

Ben nods and says he understands. He says he loves mom too. He says he will be more organized. He goes to his room and puts his toys, his books, his clothes and his mom's things in their right places. He feels proud. He thinks he is a good tester and a good organizer.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play together in the park. They also liked to do exercise. They would run, jump, and swing on the bars.

One day, they saw a big dog in the park. The dog was barking and running around. Lily and Tom were scared. They ran to the bench and hid behind it.

"Go away, dog!" Lily shouted. "You are bad!"

The dog did not go away. It came closer to the bench. It smelled Lily and Tom. It wagged its tail.

"Maybe the dog is not bad," Tom said. "Maybe it is lonely. Maybe it wants to play with us."

Lily did not think so. She was still scared. She picked up a stick and threw it at the dog. The dog caught the stick and snapped it in half. It barked again.

"See? The dog is bad!" Lily said. "It broke the stick!"

Tom felt sorry for the dog. He thought the dog was just playing. He got up from the bench and walked to the dog. He held out his hand and said, "Hi, dog. What is your name?"

The dog licked Tom's hand and wagged its tail. It looked happy. Tom smiled and petted the dog.

Lily was surprised. She did not understand why Tom was not scared. She was still hiding behind the bench. She felt troubled. She did not want to lose her best friend. She did not want to be alone.

She decided to try something. She got up from the bench and walked to Tom and the dog. She said, "Hi, dog. I am sorry I threw the stick at you. Can we be friends?"

The dog looked at Lily and wagged its tail. It licked Lily's hand and nuzzled her. Lily felt happy. She smiled and petted the dog.

Tom was glad. He said, "See? The dog is not bad. The dog is nice. The dog is our friend."

Lily and Tom hugged the dog. They played with the dog in the park. They did exercise with the dog. They ran, jumped, and swung on the bars. They had fun. They were happy.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big lion. The lion was soft and fluffy, but it had a fierce face and a loud roar. Anna and Ben liked to pretend that the lion was their friend and they went on adventures with him.

"Let's go to the jungle and find more lions!" Ben said, holding the lion in his arms.

"OK, but we have to be careful. Lions are very strong and fast," Anna said, following Ben.

They crawled under the table and made jungle noises. They saw birds, monkeys, and snakes. They had fun, but they also got tired.

"I'm sleepy. Can we nap with the lion?" Anna asked, yawning.

"Sure. The lion will keep us safe and warm," Ben said, nodding.

They lay down on the couch and cuddled with the lion. They closed their eyes and fell asleep.

Their mom came in and saw them napping. She smiled and kissed them gently. She had a gift for them. It was a book about lions and other animals. She put the book on the table and waited for them to wake up.

She knew they would love the gift and learn more about their favorite toy. She was proud of their imagination and curiosity. She loved them very much.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play outside. One day, they go to the farm with Mom and Dad. They see many animals at the farm. They see cows, pigs, chickens, and horses.

"Look, Ben, horses!" Anna says. She points to the stable. The stable is a big house for horses. It has a roof and walls, but no doors or windows. The horses can go in and out as they please.

"Can we touch them, Mom?" Ben asks. He likes horses. They are big and strong and have long hair.

"Sure, but be careful and gentle," Mom says. She holds Ben's hand and walks with him to the stable. Anna follows them with Dad.

They see a brown horse and a white horse in the stable. The brown horse is eating hay. The white horse is looking at them. The white horse has a long mane and a long tail. Anna thinks it is pretty.

"Hello, horse," Anna says. She reaches out her hand and touches the white horse's nose. The horse snorts and nudges her hand with its nose. Anna giggles.

"Can I touch your mane?" Anna asks. She moves her hand to the horse's neck and feels its long hair. The horse shakes its head and makes a sound.

"What does it say, Dad?" Anna asks.

"It says it likes you, Anna," Dad says. He smiles and strokes the horse's back.

Ben wants to touch the brown horse. He walks to the other side of the stable and sees the brown horse's ears. He touches one of the ears and pulls it gently. The horse flicks its ear and looks at Ben.

"Sorry, horse," Ben says. He lets go of the ear and touches the horse's cheek. The horse licks Ben's hand with its tongue. Ben laughs.

"Can I touch your tail?" Ben asks. He moves his hand to the horse's back and feels its long hair. The horse swings its tail and hits Ben's leg.

"Ow, horse," Ben says. He rubs his leg and backs away.

"It says it doesn't like that, Ben," Mom says. She hugs Ben and kisses his leg.

"Can we ride them, Mom?" Ben asks.

"Maybe another day, Ben," Mom says. "It's time to go home now."

Anna and Ben say goodbye to the horses. They wave their hands and thank them for letting them touch them. The horses neigh and nod their heads. Anna and Ben are happy. They had fun at the farm. They hope to come back soon.

Tom and Sue were playing with their toys in the garden. They liked to pretend they were explorers, finding new things in the world. They had a map, a compass, a binocular and a knife.

"Look, Sue, I found a big flower!" Tom said, pointing to a sunflower. "It's so yellow and pretty. I want to cut it and take it home."

"No, Tom, don't cut the flower!" Sue said. "It's alive, it needs the sun and the water. If you cut it, it will die. That's not nice."

Tom did not listen to Sue. He was ignorant. He thought he knew better. He took his knife and cut the flower. He smiled and held it in his hand.

But then, something bad happened. The flower was not just a flower. It was a home for a bee. The bee was angry that Tom cut its flower. It flew out of the flower and stung Tom on his nose.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "It hurts, it hurts, it hurts!" He dropped the flower and ran to his mom.

Sue was sad. She saw the flower on the ground, dying. She saw the bee, flying away, looking for a new home. She shook her head and said, "Tom, you were ignorant. You did not care about the world. You did not care about the flower and the bee. Now you have a bad ending."

But one day, the sun came out and the snow started to melt. Tom and Sam were sad. They wanted to keep their snow things. They started to fight over the last snowball. They threw it at each other and yelled.

"Stop it! Stop it!" their mom said. "You are making a war over nothing. The snow will melt anyway. You should share and be kind to each other."

Tom and Sam looked at their mom. They looked at the snow. They looked at each other. They felt bad. They were being mean and silly. They were making themselves and their mom miserable.

They said sorry to each other and to their mom. They hugged and smiled. They decided to play something else. They found some crayons and paper and drew pictures of snowmen, snowballs and snow forts. They had fun in the spring.

The moral of the story is: Fighting over things that don't last is foolish and unhappy. Sharing and being kind is wise and happy.

Anna liked to look at the stars at night. She had a book with pictures of the stars and planets. She learned that they were part of the universe, a big space with many things. She wanted to see more of the universe, so she asked her dad to buy her a telescope.

Dad was happy to see Anna's interest in the stars. He found a telescope online and ordered it for her. He told her it would come in a few days. Anna was very excited and counted the days.

When the telescope arrived, Anna and dad opened the box and set it up in the backyard. It was a big telescope, with a long tube and a round lens. Anna looked through the lens and saw the moon. It was bright and white, with many craters. She smiled and said, "Wow, dad, the moon is so beautiful!"

Dad smiled back and said, "Yes, it is. Do you want to see something else?" He moved the telescope and pointed it at another part of the sky. He said, "Look, Anna, that's Mars. It's a planet, like the Earth, but smaller and redder."

Anna looked through the lens and saw Mars. It was a small dot, with a faint pink color. She frowned and said, "Dad, that's not Mars. That's a pink star. Mars is bigger and redder. You made a mistake."

Dad laughed and said, "No, Anna, that's really Mars. It looks small and pink because it's very far away. The telescope makes it look closer, but not as big as the moon. Trust me, I know."

Anna did not trust dad. She thought he was lying to her. She felt angry and sad. She did not like the pink star. She wanted to see Mars. She started to cry and scream. She said, "No, no, no! That's not Mars! That's a pink star! You're wrong, dad! You're wrong!"

Anna panicked. She threw the telescope on the ground and ran into the house. She slammed the door and locked it. She did not want to talk to dad. She did not want to look at the stars. She did not like the universe. She only liked the moon.

"Here, Bear, this is for you. But be careful, it is sticky," Bee said.

Bear took the honey from Bee. He smelled it and licked it. It was sweet and yummy. He wanted to eat more.

"Thank you, Bee, this is very good. Can I have more?" Bear asked.

"Sure, Bear, you can have more. But you have to remove the wax first. The wax is not good to eat. It is hard and bitter," Bee said.

"How do I remove the wax, Bee?" Bear asked.

"You can use your claws, Bear. You can scrape the wax off the honey. Then you can eat the honey," Bee said.

Bear tried to remove the wax with his claws. But it was not easy. The wax was sticky and messy. It got stuck on his claws and his fur. He made a big mess.

"Oh, Bee, this is hard. I cannot remove the wax. It is everywhere. I am sorry, Bee," Bear said.

Bee looked at Bear. He saw the wax on his claws and his fur. He saw the honey on his face and his mouth. He saw the mess on the ground and the tree. He was not angry. He was amused.

"It is okay, Bear. You tried your best. You can keep the honey. But you have to clean yourself. You can use the water from the river. The water will wash the wax and the honey away. Then you will be clean and happy," Bee said.

"Thank you, Bee. You are a good friend. I will go to the river and clean myself. Then I will come back and play with you," Bear said.

Bee and Bear hugged. They were happy. They were friends. They liked honey.

But then, the storm came. It was very dark and loud and wet. The wind blew hard and the rain fell fast. Lily was scared. She could not see her ball. She could not see her house. She could not hear her mom. She was cold and wet and alone. She cried and cried and cried.

Her mom heard her cry. She ran outside and found her. She hugged her and said, "Lily, I am so glad you are okay. I was so worried about you. You should not have gone outside. You should have listened to me. The storm is dangerous. You could have been hurt."

Lily said, "I am sorry, mom. I was very stubborn. I complain and complain and complain. I did not obey you. I did not know what is best for me. You were right, mom. The storm is dangerous. I should have stayed inside and be safe."

Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. I love you. But you have to learn from your mistake. Next time, you have to listen to me and do what I say. I only want you to be happy and safe. Do you understand?"

Lily said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I love you too. Can we go inside now?"

Her mom said, "Yes, Lily. Let's go inside and dry off. You can play with your ball later when the storm is over."

Lily said, "Okay, mom. Thank you, mom."

They went inside and cuddled on the couch. They watched the storm pass by. They were happy and safe.

The moral of the story is: You should listen to your parents and obey them. They know what is best for you. They only want you to be happy and safe. You should not be stubborn and complain. You should be grateful and respectful.

The doctor tried to calm her down. He said he was her friend. He said he wanted to help her. He said he had a surprise for her. He reached for his pocket and took out something.

The man saw Lily. He pointed the gun at her. He pulled the trigger. Lily closed her eyes. She did not feel anything. She did not hear anything. She did not see anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy was very restless and kept running around. 

Timmy's mom noticed Billy's restlessness and suggested they build an igloo out of snow. Timmy and Billy were excited and started building the igloo. As they were building, Timmy's mom explained how an igloo keeps people warm in the cold winter. 

After they finished building the igloo, they went inside to rest. Timmy's mom brought them some hot cocoa and reminded them that it's important to take breaks and rest when we get tired. 

As they were sipping their cocoa, Timmy's mom told them a story about a little bird who didn't take breaks and worked too hard. The little bird got sick and learned that it's important to rest and take care of ourselves. 

From that day on, Timmy and Billy remembered to take breaks and rest when they got tired, just like the little bird in the story.

The lion was excited to try it out. He took the notebook and started writing all about his loudest roars. The other animals were amazed at how smart the lion had become, all because of his smelly old notebook.

Lily felt happy and full. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for the tasty pizza and the star, Mommy." Her mom hugged her back and said, "You're welcome, sweetie. Let's go home now." And they walked out of the restaurant, hand in hand.

But during the night, Lily woke up to a loud noise. She was scared and didn't understand what was happening. She called out, "Mommy, Daddy, what's going on?"

Her parents rushed into her room and explained that there was a storm outside. They hugged Lily and told her everything would be okay. Lily felt better and went back to sleep.

The next morning, Lily woke up and remembered it was her birthday. She ran to her parents' room and said, "I'm so excited! Can I open my presents now?"

Her parents laughed and said, "Not yet, Lily. First, let's have breakfast." Lily ate her breakfast and then opened her presents. She was so happy and grateful.

From that day on, whenever there was a storm, Lily didn't feel scared anymore. She understood that her parents would always be there to protect her.

Ellie was very sad that she had caused so much damage. She realized that even though she didn't mean to, her sneeze had caused a lot of trouble. From that day on, Ellie made sure to cover her nose when she felt a sneeze coming on.

Billy was very grateful for Tom's generosity and drank the gas. After drinking the gas, Billy felt much better and was ready to play.

Later that day, Tom and Billy were playing outside when they saw a man kneel down to tie his shoe. Billy asked Tom, "Why is that man kneeling?"

Tom replied, "He's tying his shoe. Sometimes we need to kneel down to do things like tie our shoes or pick up something from the ground."

Billy was amazed and said, "Wow, I didn't know that! Thanks for teaching me, Tom."

One day, they saw a very big and impressive pigeon. It had shiny feathers and a long tail. It looked like a king of the pigeons. Sam and Mia wanted to make friends with it. They threw some bread crumbs near their boat and waited for the pigeon to come.

"Hello, Mr. Pigeon," Sam said. "Do you want to play with us? We have a nice boat. You can sail with us."

The pigeon looked at Sam and Mia and the boat. It seemed curious. It walked closer to the boat and pecked at a bread crumb. Then it jumped on the boat and flapped its wings.

"Wow, he likes our boat!" Mia said. "He is a pirate pigeon!"

Sam and Mia were very happy. They made the boat sail faster and pretended to have adventures with the pigeon. The pigeon seemed to enjoy it too. It cooed and bobbed its head.

But then, something bad happened. A big gust of wind blew the boat away from the shore. Sam and Mia tried to pull the string that was attached to the boat, but it was too late. The string broke and the boat sailed farther and farther.

"Help! Help!" Sam and Mia shouted. "Our boat! Our pigeon!"

The pigeon looked scared. It tried to fly off the boat, but it was too heavy. It could not lift itself. It was stuck on the boat.

Sam and Mia cried. They did not know what to do. They had lost their boat and their new friend.

She saw the boat and the pigeon in trouble. She flew down and landed on the boat. She pecked at the string that was holding the pigeon's tail. She freed the pigeon and helped it fly.

"Thank you! Thank you!" the pigeon on the boat cooed. "You saved me!"

The queen pigeon nodded. She flew away with the pigeon. They looked happy.

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said together.

"OK, follow me. I'll show you the testing room. It's where we check if the machines are safe and strong and do what they are supposed to do."

They walked to a big room with many screens and buttons and wires. They saw different machines being tested. Some were lifted and dropped, some were twisted and bent, some were heated and cooled, some were pushed and pulled. They saw numbers and graphs and lights on the screens. They heard beeps and buzzes and clicks.

"Wow, this is amazing!" Ben said.

"How do you know what to test?" Lily asked.

"Well, we have a plan for each machine. We test different parts and functions and see if they meet the standards. We also look for any problems or errors and fix them. We want to make sure the machines are reliable and useful for our customers."

"Can we test something?" Ben asked.

"Sure, why not? Let me find something simple and fun for you. How about this toy car? It's a mini version of one of our machines. It can go fast and slow, forward and backward, left and right. It can also make sounds and lights. Do you want to try it?"

"Yes, yes, yes!" Ben and Lily said together.

"OK, here you go. Here's a remote control. You can use it to test the toy car. See how it works and have fun. But be careful, don't crash it or break it. And don't touch anything else in the room. OK?"

"OK, thank you!" Ben and Lily said.

They took the remote control and the toy car and went to a corner of the room. They turned on the car and the remote and started to test it. They made it go fast and slow, forward and backward, left and right. They made it make sounds and lights. They had a lot of fun and laughed and cheered.

They tested the toy car for a long time. They forgot about everything else in the room. They didn't notice that their dad and his friends were watching them and smiling. They were proud of their twins who liked to make things and test them. They thought they might grow up to be good engineers someday.

One day, Lily saw a sad boy in the park who had lost his toy car. She remembered how happy the ash rock made her feel, so she decided to give it to the boy. The boy was so happy and thanked Lily. As she watched him play with the ash rock, she realized that giving something to someone else can make them happy too.

She was nervous at first, but as she started to sing, she felt happier than ever before. Her friends were amazed by her talent and cheered her on.

From that day on, Lily was no longer afraid to share her talents with others. She realized that sometimes, we just need a little encouragement to overcome our fears. The moral of the story is to always believe in yourself and never be afraid to try new things.

Lily was scared, but her mommy had told her that when it's dark and scary outside, she should look for the shine. So, Lily looked up at the sky and saw a little bit of shine peeking through the clouds.

The bear nodded and said, "OK, bird. I will do that. Let's go."

The bird said, "I'm glad you like it, bear. But don't forget to attach the lid back. Or the bees will come."

The bear said, "Don't worry, bird. I will attach the lid back. I don't want the bees to sting me again."

From then on, we became good friends and would often play together in our yards. I learned that sometimes people may tell lies, but it's important to be kind and understanding.

After a few minutes of walking, they arrived at the lady's house. The old lady was very thankful to Lily for her help. She said, "Thank you so much, dear. You are very compassionate." Lily smiled and felt happy that she could help someone.

From that day on, Lily and the old lady became friends. They would meet in the park and talk about their day. Lily learned that helping others can make them happy, and that even a small act of kindness can make a big difference in someone's life.

But then, Timmy saw something scary. The big truck almost hit a little bird that was flying nearby. Timmy was sad and worried. He didn't want the bird to get hurt. So, he decided to do something. Timmy ran to the road and waved his arms to prevent the truck from going too fast. The truck driver saw Timmy and slowed down. The little bird flew away safely.

Timmy felt grateful that he could help the bird. He learned that sometimes, even little kids can do big things to help others.

Lila flew to the nearby field and brought back some fresh grass for Benny. Benny was very happy and thanked Lila for serving him the fresh grass. From that day on, Benny and Lila became good friends and helped each other whenever they needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle on a hill. The castle belonged to a very wealthy king. He had a big flag with many colors that flew high above the castle. One day, a magician appeared in front of the castle. He had a wand and a hat with a rabbit inside. 

The magician asked the king if he could perform a magic trick. The king said yes and the magician made a big rabbit appear out of his hat. The king was very impressed and gave the magician a bag of gold coins. The magician was very happy and thanked the king. 

From that day on, the magician would come to the castle every week and perform a new magic trick. The king was always amazed and gave the magician more gold coins each time. The magician became very wealthy and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely plate named Peter. He was always sad because he had no friends to play with. One day, Peter was put in the dishwasher by his owner, a little girl named Lily. 

As the dishwasher started, Peter felt scared and didn't know what was happening. Suddenly, he heard a voice coming from the other side of the dishwasher. It was a spoon named Sam. 

"Hi there, little plate! Don't be afraid, we're all in this together," said Sam. 

Peter was surprised to hear another voice and felt a little better. As the dishwasher continued to twist and turn, Peter and Sam talked about their favorite foods and how they ended up in the dishwasher. 

Finally, the dishwasher stopped and the door opened. Lily's mom came in and took out Peter and Sam. They were both clean and shiny. From that day on, Peter and Sam became best friends and were always happy to be put in the dishwasher together.

But suddenly, he heard a voice. "Hey! What do you think you're doing?" 
It was the farmer! He was getting angry. 
But the deer didn't give up. He ran away as fast as he could, with the apple in his mouth. 

The grumpy deer got away with the apple. He was so happy, he even stopped to eat it in a nearby clearing. From that day on, he always remembered to be careful when he was around people.

Ruby chased after the shadows, which moved slowly across the grass. Every time she would clap, the shadows would move faster. Eventually, she was so happy that she started spinning around!

The shadows seemed to be having fun too, because they followed her every move. Even when Ruby stopped, they kept going. It was like they had minds of their own.

Ruby and the shadows danced together until the sun went down. Then they said goodbye, until next time. Ruby clapped her hands one last time and waved to the shadow, before going inside.

She was amazed by the shiny brass ashtray and touched it carefully with her finger. She was so grateful that she had something so special in her room.

The little girl loved her ashtray so much that she decided to take it with her on all of her adventures. She would carry it carefully in her little hands, and she felt so grateful that she had found it. Everywhere she would go, she would smile and show her ashtray proudly to everyone.

The little girl and her ashtray became the best of friends and were always together. Everywhere the little girl would move, the ashtray would come too, and she was always so grateful for her special friend.

There was once a dolphin named Joe who loved to rock. One day, he was out rocking in the sea when a terrible storm came. It was so bad, the waves danced up to the sky and the wind was wild.

Joe was scared, so he decided to hide near a big rock. He waved his big flippers and rocked back and forth in the waves. He tried to stay calm and quiet, but he was so scared!

Suddenly, he heard someone calling him. It was his best friend, a fish. He told Joe to hide in the rock until the storm passed. Joe thanked the fish, and went inside the rock.

He stayed there until the storm was gone. When it was all quiet, Joe came out from his hiding place and was so happy to be safe! He slipped back into the sea and kept on rocking for the rest of the day.

But no matter how hard he tried, the cheese wouldn't budge! The mouse was very stubborn. He kept trying until his little paws were all red and sore.

Finally, he figured out the trick. He used his furry tail to grab the cheese, then squeezed it until it was soft enough to eat.

The mouse was very happy and soon ate all the cheese from the bowl. He was filled with yummy goodness!

The man kept walking and the bull followed him. When they reached a meadow, the man said it was time to rest. The bull lay down in the grass and was very happy.

The man and the bull rested in the meadow for a long time. Then, it was time to go back home. The man and the bull started to walk back, and both were very happy.

From then on, the man and the bull were the best of friends. Every day, the man would plan something special for them to do together. And no matter what, the bull was always clean and happy.

"Please banana, talk to me!" he begged.

The flower waited, and as summer turned to fall it bloomed tall and strong. When the flower had grown and was as big as the lizard, they sat together again in the sun.

The lizard said to the flower, "Now you are like me, but be patient and you can do even more. With patience, and time, you can bloom into something even bigger and more beautiful!"

The lesson of this story is that if you wait patiently, and do not rush, you can do anything in life. All it takes is patience.

This time, he tried to cross the line. But as soon as he did, he heard someone shouting at him. He looked up and saw an ignorant adult scolding him. The adult said he was not allowed to cross the line and he had to stay on the other side.

Fred didn't understand what was going on and he felt embarrassed. He ran back to the other side of the line and he vowed never to test things he didn't understand again.

Lily's mom said, "Let's go inside and clean your doll. She needs some care. And maybe Mia can play with her too, if you want to share."

Lily nodded. She said, "Okay, mom. Mia can play with her too. But only if she is nice to her."

Mia said, "I will be nice to her. I promise. Thank you, Lily."

Lily and Mia went inside and cleaned the doll. They brushed her hair, dressed her up, and sang to her. They played together and had fun. Lily was happy with her doll. And Mia learned to be a better cousin.

Anna was very happy. She was going to visit her grandma today. She loved her grandma very much. She wanted to give her a present. She saw a balloon in the store. It was red and shiny. She liked it a lot. She asked her mom to buy it for her.

"Can I have this balloon, mom?" she said.

"Sure, honey. But be careful. It is delicate. It can pop easily," her mom said.

Anna nodded. She held the balloon gently. She did not want to hurt it. She got in the car with her mom. They drove to grandma's house.

Grandma was waiting for them. She was very happy to see them. She hugged Anna and her mom.

"Hello, my darlings. I'm so glad you came to visit me," she said.

"Hello, grandma. I have a present for you," Anna said. She showed her the balloon.

"Oh, how lovely. Thank you, Anna. You are very sweet," grandma said.

She took the balloon from Anna. She smiled. She tied it to a chair. She did not want to lose it.

They had a nice time together. They talked, they ate, they played. Anna loved being with her grandma. She felt warm and cozy.

But then, something bad happened. A cat came into the room. It saw the balloon. It was curious. It wanted to play with it. It jumped on the chair. It scratched the balloon. The balloon popped. It made a loud noise.

Anna and grandma were shocked. They looked at the cat. The cat was scared. It ran away.

"Oh, no. The balloon is gone. I'm sorry, grandma. I wanted to make you happy," Anna said. She felt sad.

"It's okay, Anna. Don't be sad. The balloon was beautiful, but it was not the best present. You know what the best present is?" grandma said.

"What, grandma?" Anna said.

"You. You are the best present. You are my precious granddaughter. I love you more than anything. You make me happy just by being here," grandma said.

She hugged Anna. Anna hugged her back. She felt happy again.

"I love you, grandma. You are the best grandma ever," Anna said.

They smiled. They forgot about the balloon. They enjoyed their visit.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that the most valuable gifts are not the ones that can be bought or broken, but the ones that come from the heart, like love and kindness.

Lily was a princess who lived in a big castle. She liked to play with her dolls and dress up in pretty clothes. She had a lot of fun with her friends and family.

One day, a prince came to visit the castle. He was very handsome and polite. He brought Lily a gift of a shiny necklace. He said he wanted to marry Lily and take her to his kingdom. Lily was surprised and shy. She did not know the prince very well. She did not want to leave her home and her friends.

The prince asked Lily to come with him to his carriage. He said they had to go soon, before it got dark. Lily was scared and sad. She did not want to go with the prince. She wanted to stay with her mom and dad. She said no to the prince. She ran away to her room and locked the door.

The prince was angry and confused. He did not understand why Lily did not want to go with him. He thought she would be happy to be his wife. He knocked on the door and shouted at Lily. He said he would not leave without her. He said he would break the door if she did not open it.

Lily heard the prince's loud voice. She felt very uncomfortable. She wished he would go away and leave her alone. She hugged her dolls and cried. She hoped her mom and dad would come and help her. She did not like the prince at all. She wanted him to stop.

Lily was a little girl who loved to play with her blue ball. She would bounce it, roll it, and throw it in the air. She would take it with her everywhere she went. She thought her blue ball was the best toy in the world.

One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw some other kids playing with different toys. She saw a red bike, a yellow kite, and a green frog. They looked fun, but not as fun as her blue ball. She ran to join them and said, "Hi, can I play with you?"

The other kids looked at her and said, "Sure, you can play with us. But you have to share your blue ball. We want to try it too."

Lily felt scared. She did not want to share her blue ball. She thought it was hers and only hers. She said, "No, you can't have my blue ball. It belongs to me. Go away!"

The other kids felt sad and angry. They said, "That's not nice. You are being selfish. If you don't share, we don't want to play with you. Go away!"

Lily felt lonely and confused. She did not understand why the other kids did not like her. She hugged her blue ball and ran back to her mom and dad. She said, "Mom, dad, why don't they want to play with me? I have a blue ball. It's the best toy in the world."

Her mom and dad smiled and hugged her. They said, "Lily, we love you and your blue ball. But sometimes, it's good to share with others. Sharing makes friends. Friends make you happy. You can still keep your blue ball, but you can also let others play with it. Then, you can play with their toys too. It's more fun that way. Do you want to try?"

Lily thought for a moment. She felt a little sleepy. She said, "Maybe. But not now. I'm tired. Can we go home?"

Her mom and dad said, "Okay, we can go home. But tomorrow, we can come back to the park. And maybe, you can make some new friends. How does that sound?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "Okay. That sounds good. I love you, mom and dad. And I love my blue ball. But maybe, I can share it too."

She closed her eyes and fell asleep in her mom's arms. She dreamed of playing with her blue ball and her new friends. She felt happy.

One day, Lily wanted to lead Ben to a new game. She said, "Ben, follow me. I have a fun game for you." Ben was curious and followed Lily. Lily led him to a big tree with a hole. She said, "Look, Ben, there is a surprise in the hole. Do you want to see?"

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play near the lake. They had a small boat that they could row together. One day, they saw a big boat with many people on it. They wanted to go closer and see what was inside.

"Let's row to the big boat!" Ben said.

"OK, but be careful. The water is cold and deep." Lily said.

They rowed and rowed until they reached the big boat. They saw many things that they had never seen before. There were lights, music, food, and toys. They wanted to touch everything.

"Look, a ball!" Ben said. He reached out his hand to grab the ball, but he lost his balance and fell into the water.

"Ben!" Lily shouted. She tried to help him, but the water was too cold and the boat was too small. She started to cry.

Some people on the big boat heard her cry and came to see what was wrong. They saw Ben in the water and threw him a rope. They pulled him up and wrapped him in a blanket. They also helped Lily get on the big boat.

"Are you OK, little ones?" a kind lady asked.

"Yes, thank you." Lily said.

"What were you doing here?" a man asked.

"We wanted to see the big boat." Ben said.

"Well, you should not go near the big boat without an adult. It is dangerous. You could fall, or get lost, or get hurt. You are lucky we saw you." the man said.

"We are sorry. We did not know." Ben said.

Tim and Sam are best friends. They like to play with their cars and trucks. One day, they find a big red balloon in the park. They want to take it home.

But the balloon is tied to a bench. Tim tries to pull it, but it is too hard. Sam has an idea. He finds a rock and gives it to Tim. He says, "Use this to cut the string. Then we can have the balloon."

Tim nods and takes the rock. He rubs it on the string. The string gets thinner and thinner. Tim is careful not to pop the balloon. He looks at Sam and winks. He is almost done.

But then, a man comes to the bench. He is old and deaf. He does not hear Tim and Sam. He does not see the balloon. He sits on the bench and opens a book. He blocks the string.

Tim and Sam are scared. They do not want to lose the balloon. They do not want to make the man angry. They whisper to each other. What can they do?

Tim has another idea. He says, "I will distract the man. You release the balloon. Then we can run away."

Sam agrees. He holds the rock and the string. He waits for Tim's signal.

Tim walks to the man. He smiles and says, "Hello, sir. Do you like your book? What is it about?"

The man does not answer. He does not look at Tim. He keeps reading.

Tim tries again. He says, "Sir, can I see your book? It looks interesting. Can I read it with you?"

The man still does not answer. He does not look at Tim. He turns a page.

Tim gets closer. He says, "Sir, can I have your book? Please? I really want it. I will give it back to you."

The man finally looks at Tim. He frowns. He shakes his head. He says, "No. Go away. This is my book. Leave me alone."

Tim pretends to be sad. He says, "Okay, sir. I'm sorry. I will go away. But can I ask you one thing?"

The man sighs. He says, "What?"

Tim says, "Can you look at the sky? It is very pretty today. There are many clouds and birds. Can you see them?"

The man is curious. He says, "Really? Let me see."

He looks up at the sky. He does not see the balloon.

Tim nods at Sam. He says, "Now!"

Sam releases the balloon. He drops the rock and the string. He grabs Tim's hand. They run away.

The balloon flies up in the air. It is free. It is happy.

Tim and Sam are happy too. They have the balloon. They are best friends. They laugh and cheer. They did it.

"Wow, look at this!" Ben said. "Let's try it out!"

"Cool!" Mia said. "Can I have a turn?"

Ben shook his head. "No, it's mine. I found it first. You can play with your old boat."

Mia felt sad and angry. She wanted to play with the new boat too. She thought Ben was being mean and selfish. She looked at her old boat. It was blue and quiet and had a sail. She liked it, but it was not as fun as the new boat.

She decided to wait until Ben was not looking and then grab the new boat. She waited and waited, but Ben did not stop playing with it. He zoomed it around the tub, making waves and splashes. He did not care about Mia or her old boat.

Suddenly, something strange happened. The new boat stopped moving and started to smoke. Then, with a loud bang, it broke into pieces. Ben was shocked and scared. He dropped the button and stared at the water. His new boat was gone.

Anna nodded. "Yes, but we have to be careful. Mom said they are very old and special. We can't break them or lose them."

They put on the jewelry and pretended to be princesses. They danced and sang and had fun. But then, Lily tripped on a rug and fell down. She heard a snap.

"Oh no!" she cried. "I broke your mom's necklace! I'm so sorry, Anna!"

Anna ran to her and helped her up. She saw the broken necklace on the floor. She felt sad, but she also saw that Lily was hurt. She had a scratch on her knee.

"It's okay, Lily," Anna said. "You didn't mean to break it. Are you okay? Does your knee hurt?"

Lily nodded. "Yes, it hurts a little. But I'm more sorry about the necklace. Your mom will be mad at me."

Anna hugged her. "No, she won't. She is very friendly and nice. She will understand that it was an accident. We can tell her the truth and say sorry. Maybe she can fix it."

Lily smiled. "Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend. I'm sorry I broke your mom's jewelry."

Anna smiled back. "You're welcome, Lily. You are a good friend too. I'm glad you're okay. Come on, let's go find my mom and tell her what happened."

They held hands and walked to the living room. They hoped that Anna's mom would not be too upset. They learned that playing with jewelry was fun, but also risky. They decided to be more careful next time.
