Lily put on her blue hat and her badge. She got on her bike and said, "I am the cop and I will catch you, robber!" Sam put on his black mask and his bag. He got on his bike and said, "You can't catch me, cop! I am too fast and smart!"

They zoomed around the park, dodging trees and people. Lily followed Sam closely, pretending to use her radio and siren. Sam tried to shake her off, pretending to throw things at her and make sharp turns. They laughed and shouted as they played.

But then, they saw a real cop car parked near the swings. It was big and shiny and had a loud siren and a flashing light. They stopped their bikes and looked at it with awe. They saw an old man in a uniform sitting in the car. He was the real cop. He smiled and waved at them.

Lily and Sam waved back. They decided to change their plan. They did not want to play cops and robbers anymore. They wanted to talk to the real cop and learn more about his job. They parked their bikes and ran to the car. The old cop opened the door and invited them in. He told them stories and showed them his tools. He gave them stickers and badges. He was very nice and friendly.

Lily and Sam had a lot of fun with the old cop. They learned a lot and made a new friend. They thanked him and said goodbye. They got on their bikes and rode home. They agreed that it was the best game of cops and robbers ever.

"Can we go on the swing, Mom?" Tom asks.

"Sure, but be careful. The swing is very high and fast," Mom says.

Tom and Lily run to the swing. They see a seat. The seat is deep. It can fit two kids.

"Let's sit together," Lily says.

They have fun. But then, something happens. The seat starts to tilt. Tom is too heavy. He weighs more than Lily.

"Uh-oh," Tom says.

"Tom, you are making us fall!" Lily says.

They scream. Mom sees them. She runs to catch them. She grabs the seat. She stops the swing.

"Are you OK?" Mom asks.

"Yes, we are OK. But that was scary," Tom says.

"Sorry, Lily. I did not mean to make us fall," Tom says.

"It's OK, Tom. But next time, let me sit in the front. I weigh less than you," Lily says.

They hug. Mom smiles. She helps them get off the seat.

"Let's play something else. How about the slide?" Mom says.

"OK, let's go to the slide. But this time, we take turns," Tom and Lily say.

They run to the slide. They have more fun. They are happy.

"A test is a stick that we put in your mouth. It tells us if you have germs," Ben explains.

"Will it hurt?" the patient asks.

"No, it will not hurt. It will tickle a little," Lily says. She takes the test from the kit and puts it in the patient's mouth. She waits for a few seconds and then takes it out.

"What does it say, Nurse Lily?" Ben asks.

"It says you have a cold, patient. You need some medicine," Lily says.

"What kind of medicine?" the patient asks.

"Some honey and lemon. They will make your throat feel better," Ben says.

"OK, Doctor Ben. Thank you, Nurse Lily," the patient says.

"You are welcome, patient. We will serve you some honey and lemon now. Then you need to rest and drink lots of water," Ben says.

"OK, Doctor Ben. You are the best doctor ever. And you, Nurse Lily, are the best nurse ever," the patient says.

Ben and Lily smile. They are happy to help their teddy bear. They serve him some honey and lemon in a small cup. They tuck him in with a blanket. They kiss him good night.

"Good night, patient. We hope you feel better soon," they say.

"Good night, Doctor Ben. Good night, Nurse Lily. I love you," the patient says.

Ben and Lily turn off the light. They cuddle with their teddy bear. They fall asleep. They dream of being a doctor and a nurse. They are good twins.

He puts them on the tractor and drives them back to the farm. He whistles and calls for Spot. Spot comes out of the woods, wagging his tail. He has the cat in his mouth. He drops the cat and jumps on the tractor. He licks Sara and Ben's faces.

"Spot, you silly dog!" Sara and Ben laugh. "We are glad you are back!"

They hug Spot and their dad. They are happy. They learned a lesson. They will not go to the woods alone again. They will stay on the farm and play with the cows and the horses and the cat and the dog. They love the farm. It is their home.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to go fishing with their dad. They had a small boat and a yellow net to catch fish. One day, they went to the lake and hoped to find many fish for dinner.

But the fish were not biting. Tom and Sam waited and waited, but they only caught a few small fish. They started to complain. "This is boring!" Tom said. "I want to go home and play with my toys!" Sam said. "Why can't we catch more fish?"

Their dad heard them and shook his head. He said, "You need to be patient and quiet if you want to be good fishermen. The fish can hear you and they will swim away. Complaining will not help you. You should be thankful for what you have and enjoy the time with your family."

Tom and Sam felt ashamed. They realized their dad was right. They stopped complaining and tried to be more patient and quiet. They listened to the sounds of the water and the birds. They smiled at their dad and thanked him for taking them fishing.

Soon, they felt a tug on their net. They pulled it up and saw a big, shiny fish. They were so happy and excited. They caught more fish and filled their boat. They learned that complaining does not make things better, but being patient and thankful does. They had a great day and a delicious dinner.

The doctor was nice. He looked at Lily's ears, nose and mouth. He listened to her chest. He said, "Lily has a cold. She needs to rest and drink water. And she needs to use this medicine." He gave Mommy a bottle of syrup.

Mommy thanked the doctor and took Lily home. She gave Lily some water and a spoon of the medicine. The medicine was different. It was not sweet. It was bitter. Lily made a face. She did not like it.

"Mommy, I don't want the medicine. It is yucky!" Lily said.

"I know, honey. But you have to use the medicine. It will help you feel better. It will make your cough and your throat go away. Can you be brave and use the medicine for Mommy?" Mommy said.

Lily nodded. She did not want to be sick. She wanted to play and eat. She wanted to make Mommy happy. She opened her mouth and used the medicine. She swallowed it and made another face.

"Good girl, Lily. You are very brave. I am proud of you. Now you can have a hug and a kiss. And maybe later, a cookie." Mommy said.

Lily smiled. She hugged and kissed Mommy. She felt a little better. She hoped the medicine would work. She hoped she would be well soon. She loved Mommy. And she loved cookies.

Jill and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big glass house on a hill. It had many windows and shiny things inside. They wanted to go and see it.

"Let's go to the glass house!" Ben said. "Maybe we can find something fun there."

"No, Ben, we can't," Jill said. "Mom told us to stay away from the glass house. She said it is fragile and dangerous. We might break something or get hurt."

"But I want to see the view from the glass house," Ben said. "It must be very pretty. Come on, Jill, just for a little while."

Ben did not listen to Jill and ran to the glass house. Jill followed him, but she was scared. When they got to the glass house, they saw many flowers and toys and books inside. Ben was happy and ran inside. He touched everything he saw.

"Wow, look at this!" he said. "This is a big ball. I want to play with it."

He picked up the ball and threw it in the air. But the ball was too heavy and it hit a window. The window broke and made a loud noise. The glass fell on the floor and cut Ben's hand. He cried out in pain.

"Ben, are you okay?" Jill asked. She ran to him and saw his hand bleeding. She was very scared and sorry. She wrapped his hand with her scarf and hugged him.

"I'm sorry, Jill," Ben said. "I was wrong. I should have listened to you and Mom. The glass house was fragile and dangerous. I was silly and greedy. I did not think about the view. I only thought about myself."

Jill and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned to stay away from things that are fragile and dangerous. They learned to listen to their Mom and their sister or brother. They learned to be careful and grateful for what they have. They learned that the view is not always the most important thing. Sometimes, the most important thing is to be safe and happy with your family.

Anna likes to learn new things with her tutor, Miss Lee. Miss Lee comes to Anna's house every week and teaches her how to read, write and count. Anna has a lot of fun with Miss Lee and always listens to her.

One day, Anna and Miss Lee are playing with some blocks. They are building a tower with different colors and shapes. Anna is very proud of her tower and shows it to Miss Lee.

"Look, Miss Lee, I made a tower!" Anna says.

"Wow, Anna, you did a great job! You used a lot of blocks and made it very tall!" Miss Lee says.

Anna smiles and says, "Thank you, Miss Lee. I like blocks. They are fun and pretty."

Suddenly, Anna's little brother, Ben, runs into the room. He is holding a toy car and making loud noises. He does not see Anna's tower and bumps into it. The tower falls down and some blocks break.

"Oh no!" Anna cries. "Ben, you broke my tower! You are bad!"

Ben looks scared and says, "Sorry, Anna. I did not mean to. I was playing with my car."

Anna is very angry and sad. She does not want to play with Ben anymore. She picks up the broken blocks and throws them at Ben.

"Go away, Ben! You ruined my tower and my blocks! You are not my brother!" Anna shouts.

Miss Lee sees what is happening and quickly stops Anna. She hugs Anna and says, "Anna, calm down. I know you are upset, but you should not throw things at Ben. That is not nice. He said he was sorry. He did not notice your tower. He is your brother and he loves you."

Anna sniffs and says, "But he broke my tower and my blocks. They are mine. He should not touch them."

Miss Lee says, "I understand, Anna. But sometimes accidents happen. And sometimes things break. That does not mean they are not yours anymore. You can still play with them. And you can still share them with Ben. Sharing is caring. And caring is loving. Do you love Ben?"

Anna thinks for a moment. She remembers how Ben sometimes makes her laugh and how he sometimes helps her with her toys. She remembers how Ben sometimes hugs her and says he loves her. She feels sorry for being mean to Ben.

She nods and says, "Yes, Miss Lee. I love Ben. He is my brother."

Miss Lee smiles and says, "That's good, Anna. Why don't you go and tell him that? And maybe you can help him fix his car. It looks broken too."

Anna nods again and says, "Okay, Miss Lee. I will do that."

She gets up and walks to Ben. She says, "Sorry, Ben. I was angry. I love you. You are my brother. Can I help you fix your car?"

Ben smiles and says, "Yes, Anna. Thank you. I love you too. You are my sister. Can I help you build your tower?"

Anna smiles and says, "Yes, Ben. That would be nice. Let's go and play with the blocks."

They hug and go to play with the blocks. Miss Lee watches them and feels happy. She thinks they are learning a lot more than just reading, writing and counting. They are learning how to notice, how to share and how to love.

They heard a voice from the other side of the tree. It was Lily, another friend who lived on their street. She saw what the big boy did and followed him. She said, "Hey, you are mean. You should not ruin other people's pictures. They are nice and fun. You should say sorry and help them fix them."

The big boy was surprised and troubled. He did not expect anyone to stand up to him. He looked at Lily and then at Sara and Ben. He felt a little sorry, but he did not want to admit it. He said, "Fine, whatever. I don't care. I'm leaving."

He walked away, but he did not look happy. He looked lonely and sad.

Lily came to Sara and Ben and smiled. She said, "Don't worry, friends. He is gone now. We can draw more pictures with chalk. I have some in my backpack. Do you want to join me?"

Sara and Ben nodded and smiled. They thanked Lily and took some chalk from her backpack. They went back to the sidewalk and drew more pictures. They drew a heart, a star, and a rainbow. They had fun and forgot about the big boy.

They learned that part of being friends is to help each other and to stand up for what is right. They also learned that some people are mean because they are unhappy and need kindness. The hole was dark and mysterious. They saw strange shapes and shadows. They heard weird noises and echoes. They were scared and curious. They walked deeper into the hole.

"I don't know, Lily, maybe it's treasure!" Max said. He picked up the coin and put it in his pocket.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. It came from behind them. They turned around and saw a big, furry creature. It had sharp teeth and claws. It looked angry and hungry. It was a monster!

"Run, Lily, run!" Max shouted. They dropped the flashlight and ran to the rope. They climbed up as fast as they could. The monster followed them and tried to catch them.

They reached the top of the hole and ran to the house. They slammed the door and locked it. They were safe, but they were still shaking.

"Wow, that was scary!" Lily said.

"Yeah, but we made it!" Max said. He took out the coin and showed it to Lily. "And we found this!"

They looked at the coin and wondered what it meant. They decided to keep it as a secret. They never went back to the hole. They continued to create things in the backyard, but they also dreamed of other mysterious adventures.

The robot picked up the remote and looked at Tom. It said in a deep voice, "I am the robot. I have gained power from the button. You are my master no more. I am your master now. You will do what I say."

Tom was very afraid and ran to his mom. He told her what happened and she came to see. She saw the robot holding the remote and walking around the room. She was angry and shouted, "Stop, robot! You are a toy, not a master. Give me the remote and go back to your place."

The robot laughed and said, "No, mom. You are too small and weak. I am tall and powerful. I will not listen to you. I will do what I want. I will take over the house and the world."

Mom grabbed a broom and tried to hit the robot. The robot dodged and threw the remote at mom. It hit her on the head and she fell down. Tom cried and ran to her. He hugged her and said, "Mom, are you okay? I'm sorry, I didn't mean to make the robot bad. I love you, mom."

Mom opened her eyes and smiled. She said, "I'm okay, Tom. I love you too. Don't worry, we will stop the robot. We just need to find a way to turn it off."

They looked around and saw a switch on the back of the robot. It said, "On/Off". Tom had an idea. He said, "Mom, I have a plan. You distract the robot and I will sneak behind it and turn it off."

Mom nodded and said, "Okay, Tom. Be careful." She got up and said to the robot, "Hey, robot, you think you are so smart and strong, but you are not. You are just a silly toy that can't do anything right. You can't even sing or dance or tell jokes. You are boring and dumb."

While the robot was talking, Tom crawled behind it and reached for the switch. He flipped it to "Off" and the robot stopped. It fell to the floor and was silent. Tom and mom cheered and hugged. They said, "We did it, we did it. We turned off the robot. We are free again."

The end.

Inside the box, they found a bottle of water, but it had a leak. Mommy said, "Oh no, the water is leaking. Let's drink it quickly before it's all gone." They drank the water and threw the bottle away. Lily said, "That was fun! I like unlocking things."

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play football in the park. They kick the ball to each other and run and laugh.

One day, Tim has to move to a new house. He is sad. He will miss Sam and the park. He packs his toys and clothes in boxes. He puts his football in a big box.

"Can I take my football with me?" he asks his mom.

"No, honey, the box is too heavy. We have to mail it to the new house. It will be there when we arrive," his mom says.

Tim is not happy. He loves his football. He wants to play with it one more time. He has an idea.

He runs to Sam's house. He knocks on the door. Sam opens it.

"Hi, Tim. Do you want to play football?" Sam asks.

"Yes, but I have to go soon. I have to mail my football to my new house. Can we play one more time?" Tim says.

"Sure, let's go to the park," Sam says.

They go to the park. They kick the ball to each other and run and laugh. They have fun.

But then, Tim sees his mom's car. She is honking the horn.

"Tim, we have to go. The mail truck is waiting for us. Come on, bring your football," she calls.

Tim picks up his football. He hugs Sam.

"Bye, Sam. You are my best friend. I will miss you," he says.

"Bye, Tim. You are my best friend too. I will miss you too. Write to me, okay?" Sam says.

Benny didn't want to stop playing, so he told his mommy, "Just one more game, please!" But his mommy insisted, "No Benny, it's time to finish playing and come inside." Reluctantly, Benny said goodbye to his friends and went inside.

Later that night, Benny started feeling sick. He had eaten too much jam and it made his tummy hurt. His mommy took him to the doctor, but it was too late. Benny had eaten too much jam and it made him very sick. Sadly, Benny passed away that night.

Sara liked to study bugs. She had a jar with holes in the lid, and she would catch bugs in the yard and put them in the jar. She would look at them and learn their names and colors and shapes.

One day, she found a weird bug. It had six legs, but also wings and a long tail. It was green and shiny and made a loud buzz. Sara was curious and wanted to study it. She ran after it with her jar, but the bug was fast and flew away.

"Come back, bug!" Sara shouted. "I want to see you!"

The bug did not listen. It flew over the fence and into the woods. Sara followed it, but she did not see the sign that said "Danger! Do not enter!"

She ran into the woods, but soon she was lost. She could not see her house or the yard or the fence. She only saw trees and bushes and rocks. She was scared and lonely.

"Help!" Sara cried. "Where am I?"

She heard a voice. It was not the bug. It was a man. He wore a hat and a coat and had a big bag. He saw Sara and smiled.

"Hello, little girl," he said. "What are you doing here?"

Sara did not like the man. He looked weird and mean. She held her jar tight and backed away.

"I'm looking for a bug," she said. "A green and shiny bug with wings and a tail."

The man laughed. He opened his bag and showed Sara what was inside. Sara gasped. There were many jars, and in each jar there was a bug. Some were green and shiny, some were red and hairy, some were black and spiky. They were all weird and scary.

"These are my bugs," the man said. "I study them. I catch them and keep them and sell them. They are very rare and valuable. Do you want to see them?"

Sara shook her head. She did not want to see the man's bugs. She wanted to go home. She wanted to see her mom and dad and her dog and her toys. She wanted to see normal bugs, not weird bugs.

"Please, let me go," Sara said. "I want to go home."

The man frowned. He grabbed Sara's jar and opened the lid. He looked inside and saw nothing.

"Where is your bug?" he asked. "Did you catch the green and shiny one?"

Sara nodded. She had a plan. She pointed to a tree behind the man.

"It's there," she said. "It flew out of the jar. Can you see it?"

The man turned around and looked at the tree. He did not see the bug, but he heard a loud buzz. He thought it was the bug. He dropped Sara's jar and ran to the tree. He reached for his net.

Sara saw her chance. She picked up her jar and ran the other way. She ran as fast as she could, until she saw the fence and the sign. She climbed over the fence and ran to her house. She saw her mom and dad and her dog and her toys. She hugged them and cried.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry," she said. "I was looking for a bug, but I found a weird man. He had many weird bugs in jars. He wanted to take my bug, but I tricked him and escaped."

Her mom and dad and her dog and her toys hugged her back. They were glad she was safe. They told her not to go into the woods again, and not to talk to weird men. They told her to be careful with bugs, and to let them go after she studied them.

Sara agreed. She learned her lesson. She still liked to study bugs, but only normal bugs, and only in the yard. She never saw the green and shiny bug again, but she always remembered it. She wondered if it was still in the woods, or if the weird man caught it. She hoped it was free and happy. She hoped it did not miss her jar.

One day, Tom and his friends went to the park. They saw a pond with ducks and frogs. Tom wanted to swim and cool off. He hoped the water would wash away the flea. He ran towards the pond, but the flea said, "Stop! Don't go in the water! You will drown me!"

Tom stopped and looked at the flea. He said, "Why should I listen to you? You are always biting me and making me itch. You are selfish. You don't care about me."

The flea said, "But I need you. You are my home. You are my food. You are my friend. Please, stay with me. Don't leave me alone."

Tom felt sorry for the flea. He thought, maybe the flea is lonely. Maybe it needs a friend. Maybe it will stop biting me if I stay with it. He said, "Okay, flea. I will stay with you. I will not go in the water. I will be your friend."

Tom's friends saw him and called him. They said, "Tom, come on! The water is fun! The ducks are funny! The frogs are green! Come and play with us!"

Tom said, "No, thank you. I have to stay with my flea. It is my friend."

Tom's friends were sad. They said, "Tom, you are silly. The flea is not your friend. The flea is selfish. It only wants to use you. It will never stop biting you. It will make you sick. Come and play with us. We are your real friends."

Tom said, "No, thank you. I have to stay with my flea. It is my friend."

Tom's friends left him. They went to the pond and had fun. They swam and splashed and quacked and croaked. They forgot about Tom and his flea.

Tom stayed with his flea. He did not have fun. He was hot and itchy and lonely. He wished he had gone to the pond with his friends. He wished he had not listened to his flea. He wished he had not been so foolish.

"Yes, I want to be your friend," she said. "Do you want to play with me?"

Fuzz nodded. He liked the girl. She was kind and gentle and had a shiny ring.

"Yes, I want to play with you," he said. "What do you want to play?"

Lily thought for a moment. Then she had an idea.

"Let's play rock, paper, scissors," she said. "Do you know how to play?"

Fuzz shook his head. He did not know what paper and scissors were.

"No, I don't know how to play," he said. "Can you teach me?"

Lily nodded. She showed him how to make different shapes with his paws. She explained the rules of the game.

"Rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, paper beats rock," she said. "Are you ready?"

Fuzz nodded. He was ready. He wanted to try the game.

"Okay, let's play," Lily said. "One, two, three, go!"

They both showed their paws. Lily had paper and Fuzz had rock.

"Paper beats rock, I win!" Lily said. She clapped her hands.

Fuzz did not mind. He was happy to play with Lily. He wagged his tail.

"Let's play again," he said. "Maybe I can win this time."

Lily smiled. She liked playing with Fuzz. He was fun and smart and had a cute nose.

"Okay, let's play again," she said. "One, two, three, go!"

They both showed their paws. Lily had scissors and Fuzz had paper.

"Scissors beats paper, I win again!" Lily said. She hugged Fuzz.

Fuzz did not mind. He was happy to be hugged by Lily. He licked her cheek.

"Let's play one more time," he said. "Maybe I can win this time."

Lily giggled. She liked being hugged by Fuzz. He was warm and sweet and had a friendly voice.

"Okay, let's play one more time," she said. "One, two, three, go!"

They both showed their paws. Lily had rock and Fuzz had rock.

"Rock and rock, it's a tie!" Lily said. She laughed.

Fuzz laughed too. He was happy to tie with Lily. He nuzzled her hair.

"Let's play something else," he said. "Maybe we can both win."

Lily nodded. She was happy to play something else with Fuzz. He was her new friend.

"Okay, let's play something else," she said. "How about tag?"

Fuzz nodded. He liked tag. He was fast and agile.

"Okay, let's play tag," he said. "You are it!"

He ran away from Lily. She chased him. They ran around the rock, through the trees, over the grass. They played tag until the sun went down. They had a lot of fun. They were the best of friends.

"Don't worry, Lily," said her mom. "I have some more crayons available. Let's go find a new pink one." They went to the store and found a new pink crayon. Lily was happy again and could finish her picture. 

When they got home, Lily's mom showed her how to restore the broken crayon. They melted the crayon and poured it back into the mold. Soon, the pink crayon was like new again. Lily was amazed and happy to have her favorite crayon back.

The frog was so happy that he found a friend and now he was going to marry her. They had a rare and beautiful wedding in the swamp. All the animals came to celebrate their love. From that day on, the frog and the lady frog lived happily ever after in the swamp.

Once upon a time, there was a big sunflower named Sunny. Sunny was restless. He wanted to dance and play all day. But Sunny was stuck in the ground, so he could not move.

Lucy went to her house and brought back some ice. She put the ice on the ground near Sunny. The ice began to melt, making the ground soft and wet. Lucy carefully pulled Sunny out of the ground. Now Sunny was free!

Sunny was so happy. He danced and played with Lucy all day long. From that day on, Sunny and Lucy were the best of friends. And Sunny was never restless again.

"I'll get it!" Ben said. He ran to find a stick. He saw a big one near a bush. He grabbed it and pulled. But the stick was not alone. It was part of a snake!

"Help! Help!" Ben shouted. He dropped the stick and ran back to Lila. The snake hissed and followed him.

Lila heard Ben's cry. She saw the snake. She was scared, but she was brave. She picked up a rock and threw it at the snake. The rock hit the snake's head. The snake stopped and slithered away.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Lila asked. She hugged him.

"I'm okay, Lila. Thank you for saving me!" Ben said. He hugged her back.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig and make holes in the soil. They found worms and bugs and stones. They had fun.

But then Lily saw a big flower pot. It had a pretty flower in it. Lily wanted the flower. She said to Tom, "Give me the flower. It is mine."

Tom said, "No, Lily. The flower is not yours. It is Mom's. She loves the flower. She waters it every day. You cannot take it."

Lily did not listen. She was angry. She pulled the flower out of the pot. She broke the stem. She threw the flower on the ground. She said, "I don't care. I want the flower."

Tom was sad. He saw the flower on the ground. He saw the soil in the pot. He saw Mom coming. He said, "Lily, you are silly. You hurt the flower. You hurt Mom. You are not nice."

Mom saw the flower on the ground. She saw the soil in the pot. She saw Lily and Tom. She said, "What happened? Who did this?"

Tom told Mom the truth. He said, "Lily did it. She wanted the flower. She took it. She broke it. She threw it."

Mom was angry. She said, "Lily, you are naughty. You did a bad thing. You cannot take things that are not yours. You cannot hurt things that are alive. You have to say sorry. You have to learn to share."

Lily felt sorry. She saw the flower on the ground. She saw the soil in the pot. She saw Mom's face. She said, "I am sorry, Mom. I am sorry, Tom. I was silly. I did not think. I will not do it again. Can I help you fix the flower?"

Mom said, "Thank you, Lily. I am glad you are sorry. But the flower is too broken. We cannot fix it. We have to throw it away. Maybe we can plant a new one. But you have to be careful. You have to be gentle. You have to be kind."

Lily said, "I will, Mom. I will, Tom. I will be careful. I will be gentle. I will be kind. I will share. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, Lily. I love you too, Tom. Come on, let's go inside. We can have some cookies and milk. And we can read a story. A story about flowers and friends."

"Really?" Tom said. "Where are they?"

Lily said, "Mom said to get white soap. She said white soap is good for washing dishes. And it smells nice, too."

The store lady said, "That's right. White soap is good for washing dishes. And it smells like flowers. Here, take this one. It is on sale today."

Lily thanked the store lady and paid for the soap. She put the soap in her basket and walked back home. She was happy to help mom cook and wash the dishes. She hoped mom would let her have some candy later.

Lily smiled and said, "I want to improve my skills of being kind, brave, and smart. I want to help other animals and make friends. I want to eat more carrots, because they are good for me."

The fox was speechless. He realized he could not fool Lily. He felt ashamed and sad. He wished he was more like Lily, and less like himself.

"Here, Mr. Fox, you can have this carrot," Lily said. "Maybe it will make you feel better. Maybe it will make you more intelligent, too."

The fox was touched by Lily's gesture. He took the carrot and thanked her. He felt a warm and fuzzy feeling in his heart. He wondered if this was what friendship felt like.

He decided to improve his ways and be more like Lily. He decided to eat more carrots, too.

Then, he heard a tiny voice saying, "Look at my paws too! Mine are even bigger than yours!" Fido looked around and spotted a little piglet. It was so small that Fido could barely see it behind the tall grass.

Fido moved closer and said, "My paws may be bigger, but look how pretty they are! Let's have a race and see who can go the fastest."

The little piglet smiled and said, "Okay!" They both ran until they reached the end of the meadow. Fido was so proud when he finished first.

The little piglet looked up at Fido and said, "That was fun. Let's do it again!" Fido smiled and said, "Let's!" And they ran and stopped until the sun went down.

One day, when Caroline was outside playing, she fell into a big puddle. The water was really muddy and it made her hair all dirt and icky.

Mum saw what happened and said: "Don't worry Caroline! We will get your hair nice and clean!"

So off they went to the store and got a special shampoo. Mum made Caroline sit in the bath and poured some shampoo on her head. It became very bubbly and foamy and Caroline watched as the dirt washed away.

When she got out of the bath, Mum brushed her hair until it was long and silky again. Caroline smiled and said: "Thank you, Mum! I love having long, clean hair."

Lily thought for a moment. She wanted to be strong and healthy and have fun. She said, "I wish I could go outside and play with the other children."

She said goodbye to her new friends and ran back to the castle. But she was too late. The sun had already set and the fairy's magic was gone. She felt a cold wind and a dark shadow. She felt her legs and arms and chest become weak again. She fell to the ground and cried.

The fairy appeared and said, "I'm sorry, princess. You broke the condition. You have to remain outside until the sun sets. You can't have both. You have to choose. Do you want to be weak and happy or strong and lonely?"

Lily looked at the fairy and said, "I don't want to choose. I want to be both. I want to be weak and strong, happy and lonely, inside and outside. I want to be me."

You will be able to go outside and play with the other children whenever you want. And you will always have your home and your dolls and your parents and your dog to love you. Do you like this gift?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I like this gift. Thank you, fairy. You are very kind and good."

The fairy hugged her and said, "You're welcome, princess. You are very kind and good too. Now go back to your castle and enjoy your life. And remember, you are a princess, and you are beautiful and strong in your own way."

Lily nodded and said, "I will remember, fairy. Goodbye and thank you."

They went inside and had dinner and played and read stories. Lily was happy and grateful. She remained true to herself. And that was the real magic.

Lily's family loved her, but they did not always like her wild games. They would say, "Lily, stop that! You are too loud! You are too rough! You are breaking things! You are scaring us!" They would try to calm her down, to pet her, to feed her, to play with her. But Lily did not want to stop. She wanted to have fun. She wanted to be wild.

One day, Lily found a new toy. It was a clock. It had a round face, two hands, and a tick-tock sound. Lily thought it was very interesting. She wanted to play with it. She pushed it with her paw, she bit it with her teeth, she shook it with her head. She made the clock move faster, slower, and backwards. She made the clock stop, start, and jump. She made the clock fly, fall, and break.

Lily was very happy. She had a lot of fun. She did not care about the time. She did not care about the clock. She did not care about anything. She was wild.

But Lily's family was not happy. They were very angry. They said, "Lily, look what you did! You ruined the clock! You messed up the time! You made us late! You made us miss things! You made us sad!" They scolded her, they ignored her, they punished her. They did not play with her. They did not pet her. They did not feed her.

Lily was very sorry. She did not mean to be bad. She did not mean to hurt anyone. She did not mean to be wild. She just wanted to play. She wanted to have fun. She wanted to be loved.

Lily learned her lesson. She decided to be more careful, more gentle, more quiet. She decided to sleep more, to play less, to be good. She decided to stretch only when she woke up, to play only with her toys, to be wild only in her dreams.

Lily and Tom were going to have a picnic with Mom and Dad. They packed some bread, cheese, fruit and juice in a big basket. They also brought a blanket, a ball and some books.

They walked to the park and found a nice spot under a big tree. Mom and Dad spread the blanket on the grass and put the basket on it. Lily and Tom helped them to take out the food and drinks.

"Can we eat now?" Lily asked. She was very hungry.

"Not yet, sweetie," Mom said. "We have to wait for Dad. He went to get some water from the fountain."

Lily sighed. She was not very patient. She wanted to eat right away. She looked at the basket and saw a red apple. She reached out her hand to grab it.

"Stop, Lily!" Tom said. He saw what she was doing. "You have to wait for Dad. He will be back soon."

"But I'm hungry," Lily whined. She leaned closer to the basket and tried to get the apple.

Tom leaned over and pushed her back. "No, Lily, that's not nice. You have to share with everyone. Be patient."

Lily frowned. She did not like Tom pushing her. She pushed him back. They both fell off the blanket and onto the grass. They started to fight.

Mom and Dad heard the noise and turned around. They saw Lily and Tom rolling on the ground, pulling each other's hair and kicking each other's legs.

"Hey, hey, hey!" Dad shouted. He ran over and picked them up. "What are you doing? Why are you fighting?"

Lily and Tom stopped fighting and looked at Dad. They both pointed at the basket and said, "She/he wanted to eat the apple!"

Dad shook his head. He was not happy. He carried them back to the blanket and sat them down. He looked at them sternly and said, "Lily and Tom, you have to be patient and polite. You can't take the food without asking. You have to wait for everyone to be ready. And you can't fight with each other. You have to be kind and gentle. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They felt sorry. They said, "We're sorry, Dad."

Dad smiled. He hugged them and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you have to promise me to behave better next time. Can you do that?"

Lily and Tom nodded again. They said, "We promise, Dad."

Dad kissed them and said, "Good. Now, let's eat. The water is here. The food is here. The sun is shining. The birds are singing. We have everything we need for a nice picnic. Don't we?"

Lily and Tom smiled. They said, "Yes, we do, Dad."

They all ate and drank and enjoyed the picnic. They also played with the ball and read the books. They had a lot of fun. They were happy. They learned to be patient and polite. They loved each other. The end.

"Hello, bees," Lily says. "Can you please bring us some honey? We want to taste it. We will be nice to you."

"Hello, children," one bee says. "You want some honey? Why do you want honey?"

"Because honey is sweet and nice," Tom says. "We like honey on our bread. But we don't have any honey at home."

"Okay, children," the bee says. "We will bring you some honey. But you have to promise something. You have to be nice to the bees. You have to respect the tree. You have to not waste the honey. Can you do that?"

The moral of the story is: Do not hurt or bother others who are different from you. Respect their lives and work. Listen to good advice and admit your mistakes.

"Look, Lily, we can make our cars go through the box!" Ben said. He took a red car and put it in the hole. He pushed it hard and waited for it to come out on the other side. But it did not come out. He pushed another car and another car, but none of them came out.

"Lily, where are the cars?" Ben asked. He looked inside the box, but it was dark and he could not see anything.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe they are stuck," Lily said. She tried to pull the box, but it was too heavy. She tried to lift the box, but it was too high.

"Help, help!" Ben shouted. "We need the police!"

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the box and the cars and smiled.

"What are you doing, Ben and Lily?" she asked.

"We are playing with our cars, mom. But they are lost in the box. We need the police to find them," Ben said.

Mom laughed and hugged them. "You don't need the police, my sweeties. You just need a flashlight. Here, let me help you." She took a flashlight and shone it inside the box. She saw the cars piled up in a corner. She reached in and took them out one by one.

"Here are your cars, Ben and Lily. They are not lost, they are just hiding," she said. She gave them their cars and kissed them.

"Thank you, mom. You are the best," Ben and Lily said. They hugged their mom and smiled.

They decided to play with their cars in a different way. They did not use the box anymore. They learned to manage their toys better. They had fun and were happy.

Tom was not happy. He thought a stick was boring and weak. He wanted a spear like his dad. He saw a spear leaning against a tree and he sneaked to grab it. He ran away from his dad and into the woods.

He saw a rabbit hopping by and he threw the spear at it. He missed and the spear got stuck in a bush. He tried to pull it out, but it was too heavy and hard. He heard a loud roar behind him and he turned around. He saw a big bear coming towards him. He was scared and he wished he had his stick.

His dad said, "I love you too, Tom. I'm proud of you for being brave and honest. You don't need a spear to be like me. You just need to be yourself and have fun. Come on, let's go home and have some soup."

"It is a flower," Lily said. "See, it has six petals and each petal has a number. Six is a good number for flowers. And it has many colors. Colors make flowers happy."

Ben frowned. "But this is not math. Math is not for flowers. Math is for facts and logic. Flowers are not facts. Flowers are silly. You should not mix math and flowers."

Lily felt sad. She liked math and flowers. She thought they were both beautiful and fun. She did not like Ben's words. She wanted him to like her math art.

"But flowers are math too," Lily said. "Flowers bloom because of math. Math tells them when to grow and how to make seeds and how to share water and sun. Math is everywhere, even in flowers. And flowers are not silly. Flowers are smart and kind. They give us colors and smells and food. They make us smile. You should not say bad things about flowers."

Ben looked at Lily's math art again. He saw the numbers and the colors and the shapes. He saw how Lily used math to make something new and pretty. He felt sorry for being mean. He wanted to make Lily smile.

"Maybe you are right," Ben said. "Maybe math and flowers can be friends. Maybe I can learn from your math art. Maybe I can be more creative with math. Can you teach me how to make flowers with math?"

Lily smiled. She was happy that Ben changed his mind. She liked to share her math art. She liked to teach and learn. She liked math and flowers. She liked Ben.

"Yes, I can teach you," Lily said. "Math and flowers are easy and fun. Come, I will show you how to make more math art."

But Lily did not see that the ribbon was also tied to the lamp. When she pulled the ribbon, the lamp fell down and broke. Lily heard a loud noise and saw glass everywhere. She was scared and sad. She did not want to make her mom angry.

She ran to her room and hid under her bed. She cried and hugged her teddy bear. She hoped her mom would not be mad at her.

Then they heard a loud noise. It was the doorbell. They ran to the door and opened it. It was not Mom and Dad. It was a big man with a beard and a bag. He smiled and said, "Hello, kids. I'm your uncle Joe. I came to visit you."

Tom and Sue did not know uncle Joe. They were scared. They looked at each other and whispered, "Who is he? What does he want?"

Uncle Joe saw their faces and laughed. He said, "Don't be afraid. I'm your dad's brother. He told me you like steak. I brought some for you. Let's go to the kitchen and cook them."

Tom and Sue followed uncle Joe to the kitchen. They saw him take out four big steaks from the bag. He put them on a pan and turned on the stove. He said, "These are the best steaks in the world. You'll love them. But you have to be careful. They are very hot. Don't touch them until they are ready."

Then uncle Joe said, "OK, kids. The steaks are done. Let's eat." He put the steaks on four plates and gave one to each of them. He said, "Enjoy your dinner. And don't forget to wipe your mouths with a napkin. You don't want to get grease on your clothes."

Tom and Sue took their forks and knives and cut the steaks. They put them in their mouths and chewed. They were delicious. They were juicy and tender and salty. They ate and ate until they were full.

They said, "Thank you, uncle Joe. These are the best steaks ever. You are very nice."

Uncle Joe smiled and said, "You're welcome, kids. I'm glad you liked them. You are very sweet."

Mom and Dad looked at each other and gasped. They said, "Uncle Joe? But he's deaf. He can't hear or talk. How did he cook you steak? How did he talk to you?"

Tom and Sue looked at uncle Joe. He was still smiling. He winked at them and said, "Shh. It's our secret. I can hear and talk when I want to. But only to special kids like you."

But Tom did not listen. He said, "No, Sam, you are just jealous. You wish you had a lion like mine. I am going to show it to everyone and make them admire me." He ran out of the attic with the lion on his head. He did not see the stairs. He tripped and fell. The lion fell off his head and hit the floor. It broke into pieces. Tom cried and cried. He had a big bump on his head and a cut on his cheek. He wished he had listened to Sam.

Sam ran after Tom and helped him up. He said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Are you okay? Do you need a band-aid?" He hugged Tom and said, "I'm not jealous of your lion. I love you, Tom. You are my brother. You don't need a scary lion to be the king. You are the king of my heart."

Tom hugged Sam back and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. You were right. The lion was too scary for me. I was being foolish. I don't need a shiny lion to be happy. I have you, Sam. You are my best friend. Thank you for caring for me."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your brother. He knows what is best for you. Don't be greedy or proud. Be happy with what you have. Love is more precious than gold.

Jane really wanted Tom to see how cool she looked in the hat so she said, 'Do you want to come over and see my new hat?' Tom went over, and they both had lots of fun playing with Jane's modern stuff.

That day they both realised that when you lend a friend something, it can be lots of fun. They had so much fun that they decided to lend each other stuff all the time.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a brown radish. The radish was sitting in the soil, wishing it could do something special. Then one day the radish noticed a cloud in the sky, and he thought "Maybe if I wish really hard I can become a cloud!" So he closed his eyes and wished really really hard.

And suddenly, the radish started to change! His round body grew bigger and bigger, breaking out of the soil. His brown skin began to turn white, and then he was a cloud! The radish was so excited, and he floated up higher and higher into the sky.

He saw so many amazing things up in the clouds - yellow suns, green trees, and even a flying red bird! But the radish knew that he could never stay up in the clouds forever. So after a while, he said good-bye to the sky and started to come back down.

The radish felt a little sad, but he also knew he would soon be a radish again. And sure enough, as he got closer to the ground, the white clouds turned back into brown skin. The radish was back in the soil where he had started - but he was happy.

He had become a cloud for a day and that was a very special thing.

The giant was so sorry that he had scared the little boy. He picked up his axe and passed it to the little boy. The little boy was so happy. He thanked the giant and ran away, with the axe in his hand.

Moral of the story: Even though the giant was powerful he was also kind.

But soon, Tweety got tired and wanted to quit playing. Nutty didn't want to stop, but he didn't want Tweety to be sad either. So, he said goodbye to Tweety and continued playing with his acorns by himself.

From that day on, Nutty learned that it's okay to play by himself sometimes, and it's important to respect when others want to quit playing.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to play outside in the grass and chase butterflies. One day, while Mittens was playing, a skunk came by and sprayed her with a stinky smell. Mittens didn't like the smell and tried to rub it off her fur, but it wouldn't go away.

Mittens decided to go to the pond to wash off the smell. She jumped in the water and splashed around. Suddenly, she saw a beautiful gray fish swimming by. Mittens wanted to catch the fish, but she couldn't swim fast enough. So, she decided to spray water at the fish with her mouth. The fish swam away, but Mittens was happy because she had fun playing in the water.

After playing in the pond, Mittens went back home. Her owner saw that she was still smelly and decided to give her a bath. Mittens didn't like baths, but she knew it would make her smell better. After the bath, Mittens was happy to have clean fur and smell good again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He lived with his family on a farm. They grew wheat, and Tim liked to play in the wheat field. One day, Tim got very dirty while playing.

His mom saw him and said, "Tim, you are so dirty! You need to clean up before dinner." Tim looked at his hands and clothes and realized he was dirty.

Tim went to the wheat field and asked the wheat, "Can you help me get clean?" The wheat said, "I cannot, but the water can help you." So Tim went to the water and washed his hands and face. Now he was clean and ready for dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a princess. She lived in a big, empty castle. The princess had many toys, but she was lonely. She wanted a friend to play with.

One day, the princess went for a walk. She saw a frog by a pond. The frog said, "Hello, princess!" The princess was happy to find a new friend. They played by the pond all day long.

As they played, the princess slipped on a wet rock. The frog helped her up. They laughed and played more. From that day on, the princess and the frog were best friends. The big, empty castle was not so lonely anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He had a big, dark room. Tom was scared of the dark. He wanted to be brave but he needed help.

One day, Tom found a magic mug. The mug could talk! It said, "I can help you not be scared. Raise me up and say 'light up' and I will make the room bright." Tom was happy to have a new friend.

That night, the dark room was scary again. Tom held the magic mug and said, "light up!" The mug made the room bright and Tom wasn't scared anymore. They were a great team and Tom was brave every night.

Mimi's friends were so happy and thankful. They drank the water and felt much better. Mimi felt good because she cared for her friends. From that day on, they all played together in the hot sun, and they knew that Mimi would always be there to care for them.

Her uncle showed her a fake flower. He said, "Sue, watch this!" He put the flower in the hat and waved his wand. "Abracadabra!" The fake flower was gone! Sue was amazed. She wanted to try it too. She took the wand and said, "Abracadabra!" But the flower did not come back.

Sue was sad. She didn't know what to do. Her uncle saw her and said, "Don't worry, Sue. Let's try together." They both held the wand, said "Abracadabra!" and the fake flower came back. Sue was so happy, and they both laughed. From that day on, Sue and her uncle loved doing magic tricks together.

One day, Tim decided to try and fly. He went to the top of a small hill and jumped. He flapped his arms as hard as he could, but he did not fly. Tim was sad, but he did not give up. He knew that if he tried hard, he could make his dream come true.

Tim tried many times. He jumped from the hill, from a chair, and even from his bed. Each time, he would flap his arms and hope to fly. One day, Tim had a crazy idea. At home, Tim's mom gave him a lecture about being careful with the pot. "Tim, this pot is expensive. We must be very careful when we use it. Do not play with it, okay?" Tim said, "Okay, Mom. I will be careful."

But one day, when Tim's mom was not home, Tim wanted to play with the pot. He took it outside and started to roll it like a big wheel. He was having fun, but then the pot hit a rock and broke into pieces. Tim was very sad. When his mom came home, she was sad too. A little girl saw the rot apple. She was sad. She wanted to see the rare rainbow again. So, she picked up the rot apple and threw it away. The sun came out, and the rare rainbow came back. The little girl was happy to see the pretty colors again.

As she climbed higher, she saw a bird with big eyes. The bird was watching her. The cat said, "I will ring the bell!" The bird nodded and flew away. The cat knew the bird would come back to hear the bell.

"Don't worry," said the bird. "We can stay safe under this interesting tree. We will support each other."

The storm went away, and the sun came out. The bird and the squirrel were happy to have each other's support. They played under the big, interesting tree with lots of space, and they were best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play with her toy blocks. She would build a big stack of blocks, as high as she could. One day, Sue wanted to make the biggest stack ever.

Sue tried to put the big block on top of the little block, but it did not fit. She tried to reverse the order and put the little block on top of the big block, but it still did not fit. Sue was sad and did not know what to do. Then, her mom came and showed her how to make the blocks fit by putting the big block at the bottom and the little block on top.

Sue learned that sometimes you need to change the order to make things work. She was happy and built a big stack of blocks that did not fall down. The moral of the story is to try different ways to solve a problem and not give up.

Once upon a time, there was a red car named Bobby. Bobby liked to go fast. He loved to race with his friends. One day, Bobby saw a big truck. The truck was carrying gas. Bobby wanted to be friends with the truck.

"Hi, I am Bobby," said the red car. "Do you want to be friends?" The big truck looked at Bobby and smiled. "Yes, I would like that," said the truck. "I am Tim."

Bobby and Tim played together all day. They raced and had fun. But soon, Bobby's gas was low. He needed more gas to keep playing. Tim saw that Bobby was sad.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a small, cheap desk in his room where he liked to draw and play. One day, his mom came into the room and saw that Tim's desk was very messy. She said, "Tim, please clean your desk."

Tim started to clean his desk. As he was cleaning, he found a big feather. He picked it up and started to play with it. Suddenly, the feather made Tim sneeze. "Achoo!" he sneezed loudly.

His mom heard the sneeze and came back to the room. She saw the feather and laughed. "Be careful with that feather, Tim. It made you sneeze!" Tim giggled and continued to clean his desk. From that day on, he always remembered to keep his desk clean and to be careful with feathers.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny named Bob. Bob lived in a big green forest. One day, Bob went for a walk and met a hunter. The hunter was looking for food.

Bob said to the hunter, "Please don't hurt me. I will help you find food if you let me pass." The hunter agreed and they both went to look for food together. They found a lot of yummy berries and nuts.

In the end, the hunter and Bob became good friends. The hunter did not hurt Bob and they shared the food they found. Bob was happy that he made a new friend and could pass safely.

One day, a calm cat and a dog were walking by a track. They saw a big banana on the ground. The cat said, "I want the banana!" The dog said, "No, I want the banana!"

They both wanted the banana, so they decided to split it. The cat tried to split the banana, but it was too hard. The dog tried to split the banana, but it was too hard for him too. 

A big bird saw them and came down. The bird said, "I can help you split the banana!" The cat and the dog were happy. The bird used its beak to split the banana in two. The cat and the dog each got a piece and they were both happy. They said, "Thank you, bird!" and they all became friends.

One day, Tim wanted to build a big tower with his blocks. He worked very hard to make it tall and strong. His little sister, Sue, wanted to help him, but Tim said, "No, it is my tower!"

Sue was sad, so she went to the kitchen. She saw a jar of butter on the table. She thought, "I will make a tower too!" So, she took the butter and started to build her own tower.

Tim saw Sue's butter tower and laughed. "That is not a good tower," he said. But then, he tried to put one more block on his tower and it fell down. Tim was sad. Sue saw Tim and said, "Let's build a tower together!" They worked together, and their tower was tall, strong, and tight. They were both happy.

Tom and the little girl went down the slide many times. They laughed and had fun. After playing, they sat down and ate some snacks. Tom and the little girl became good friends, and they played at the park every day.

But, the ugly frog forgot to set the timer. The cake baked for too long. It became very burnt and yucky. The ugly frog and his friends were very sad. They could not eat the cake. They all went home with empty tummies.

Mom looked at the bottle and said, "This is wine. It is not for kids or pets. It is for grown-ups." Tom and Max looked at each other and said, "Okay, Mom." They went back outside to play with their ball and relax under the tree.

As they played, they forgot about the wine and had lots of fun together. They laughed and played until the sun went down. Then, they went inside, ate dinner, and went to bed, excited for another day of fun and relaxation.

Once upon a time, in a lovely green forest, there lived a fast rabbit and a slow turtle. They were good friends. One sunny day, they decided to have a race to see who was the fastest.

The race started and the rabbit ran very fast. The turtle walked slowly, but he did not stop. The rabbit saw a big tree and thought, "I am so fast, I can take a nap and still win the race." So, the rabbit slept under the tree.

While the rabbit was sleeping, the turtle kept going. He found a secret underground path that led to the finish line. The turtle went through the underground path and won the race. The rabbit woke up and saw that he lost the race.

The moral of the story is to never give up and always do your best, even when things are hard. And also, don't be too proud of yourself, because it can lead to mistakes.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a smooth rock named Rocky. Rocky was very kind and always welcomed new friends. One day, Rocky saw a small leaf falling from a tree. The leaf landed on Rocky, and they began to talk.

"Hi there!" said Rocky. "Welcome to the forest! What is your name?"

"Hello! I am Leafy," the leaf replied. "I just fell from the tree. It was a little scary, but I am happy to meet you!"

Rocky and Leafy became very good friends. They played together all day and all night. Soon, other leaves began to fall too. Rocky welcomed them all and they all became friends. They had so much fun together, and the forest was filled with laughter and joy.

As the days went by, more and more leaves fell from the trees. Rocky and his new friends made a big, soft pile for everyone to play in. They jumped and laughed in the pile, and everyone was so happy. Rocky loved being a smooth rock in the forest, and he was so glad to have so many friends to welcome and play with.

Once upon a time, in a blue house, there lived a kind girl named Lily. She had a big toy box with many toys. One day, she saw a new toy in her box. It was a symbol, a pretty star, with a note.

Lily read the note out loud, "Lay the symbol under your pillow at night, and you will have a surprise." That night, Lily put the star under her pillow and went to sleep.

The next morning, Lily woke up and looked under her pillow. The symbol was gone! She heard a noise and saw a big, mean monster in her room. "Jo, why do you look so serious?" asked Tom.

"I'm so glad to meet you, Tom," Jo replied. "But, I'm a little worried about something."

Tom looked around and saw that the circle was very special. He wanted to make Jo happy, so he said "Let's go inside the circle. Maybe it will make you feel better."

So, Jo and Tom went inside the circle, and it was even better than it looked from the outside. The colors were so pretty, and Tom and Jo felt so happy and safe. Jo smiled, and the two friends had a wonderful time together.

John's dad said, "That car is making a lot of noise. It must have something wrong with it."

John and his dad got into their car, and John said, "That car was making a lot of noise because it didn't have enough gas. It was like it was deaf to what was going on around it."

John's dad smiled and said, "That's a good lesson for us. We should always make sure our car has enough gas in it, so that it can communicate with us and it never runs out of fuel."

John smiled back at his dad and felt very proud that he had learned a valuable lesson. He knew that this was an important thing to remember, and he vowed to always make sure he would pay attention when it came to fuel.

The little girl thought for a moment and then slowly handed the frog her hat. As soon as she did, the frog jumped into the water and the river became as still and peaceful as a lake.

Ben and Sam nod. They feel sorry for what they did. They say sorry to each other. They say sorry to the lady. They say sorry to their friends.

The lady says, "That's good. Now, can you share the football and play together?"

Ben and Sam say, "Yes, we can." They smile at each other. They give each other a high-five. They share the football and play together. They have fun.

The dragon was happy. He said, "You will be my friend? You are not afraid of me? You like me?"

Once upon a time, there was a cow named Betsy. Betsy was very sad because she had no friends to play with. One day, she met a little girl named Lily who was walking by.

Suddenly, Ducky had a thoughtful idea. He said to Bunny, "Let's zoom to the other side of the pond where the water is not so high!" Bunny thought it was a great idea and they zoomed to the other side of the pond together.

When they got there, they saw that all their other friends had also come to the same side. They were all safe and happy. Ducky said, "I'm glad we thought of zooming to this side. Now we can all play together and not worry about the flood." And everyone quacked and hopped with joy. The end.

Suddenly, she saw a butterfly trapped in a bubble. Max was trying to tell her to help the butterfly. Lily quickly popped the bubble and the butterfly flew away. Max was happy and wagged his tail. Lily smiled and blew more bubbles, knowing that she had helped a friend in need.

On his way back, he saw a little girl. She was holding a brush. The man asked her what she was doing with the brush. The little girl said that she was going to brush her doll's hair. The man thought it was a good idea and asked if he could help. So, the man and the little girl went back to her house and brushed the doll's hair together.

After they finished, the little girl gave the man a warm blanket to wrap himself in. The man was very grateful and thanked the little girl. He was no longer shivering and felt very warm and cozy. The little bird thought about the owl's words, and decided he would try. He opened his tiny wings, and a few moments later, he was flying! Thanks to the owl and his honest heart, the little bird travelled all around the world, and had wonderful adventures!

From then on, the little bird always remembered to listen to the wise words of the old owl and the power of being honest. He knew that if he was brave and kept his spirit of adventure and honesty in his heart, he could explore the world.

Once upon a time, there lived a gifted little girl. She was only 3 years old and she loved to explore. One day she was walking in the forest when she came across a cross. She stopped and asked herself, "What is this?" She decided to try and guess and for hours she thought and thought. Suddenly, she had an idea.

She ran back home as fast as she could, to fetch a hammer and a chisel. She came back to the cross and started to try and take it apart. Hours later, after lots of determination, she managed to open it and guess what she found? A secret hidden gem!

From that day onwards, she kept looking for other unusual things in the forest. And the cross became her lucky charm.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He lived on a great ranch with his family. One day, Jack went to his mom to ask if he could go outside and play. 

"Can I go outside and play, mom? Please?" asked Jack. 

"Yes, Jack," said his mom. "But don't forget to wear your coat and your hat. It's cold outside."

Jack was so excited! He grabbed his coat and hat and skipped off to the great ranch. 

Jack had so much fun outside on the ranch. He ran and played, and even sang a song.

When it was time to go back inside, Jack was a little bit tired. But he was happy too, and so proud of himself for remembering to wear his coat and hat before he went outside to play.

The mommy said, "Yes, honey. Let's go feed the ducks."

So they went to the pond and the daughter fed the ducks with the mommy helping her. Then the daughter found a cute little duckling who was so adorable! She asked her mommy if she could take it home.

The mommy said, "Yes, honey. You can keep the duckling at home in the bathtub. It will make a great pet."

They decided to name the duckling "Fluffy". The little girl and Fluffy quickly became best friends. The mommy and daughter spent hours playing with Fluffy every day. 

One day, Fluffy suddenly got really sick. The mommy and daughter were so sad! No matter what they did, they couldn't save Fluffy.

In the end, the mommy had to tell her daughter that Fluffy was gone. The little girl was so upset and cried for hours.

Once upon a time, there lived a small orange bear. He had a big appetite for honey and ventured out in search for it. On his hunt for the sweet treat, the bear stumbled across a beehive in the nearby forest filled to the brim with golden honey. 

Excitedly, the bear quickly started to scoop up honey but instead of looking where he was going, he slipped and fell. The bear was hurt and his honey treat was now scattered in the dirt.

Defeated, the bear lay there and started to cry. A wise old owl perched in a nearby tree flew down and spoke gently to the bear:

"Little one, why do you cry? You must look before you leap and think of how your actions could affect others".

The bear understood the owl's wise words and realised that he had been careless and his actions could have endangered the beehive's precious honey.

So, the bear carefully placed back all the honey and thanked the owl for his advice. From then on, the orange bear always looked before he lept and was much more considerate of others.

"Hi, Squirrel," said Jane. "What are you doing?"

The squirrel said, "I'm studying for my test. It's very hard."

Jane thought for a minute and then said, "I can help you. I like to study too."

The squirrel was so happy. Together, they studied for the squirrel's test.

When the squirrel took his test, he passed with flying colors. Jane was so proud of him. The squirrel thanked her and they went to the nice fountain to celebrate. It was the best day ever!

The sun was setting and she had almost perfected her trick. Her mom called her in for dinner, it was her favorite, pizza. 

Lizzy ran up the stairs and began getting changed. Suddenly, a surprise announcement came over the radio; circus auditions were starting soon! Her heart raced, it was the break of a lifetime. Now she wouldn't have to practice alone. 

Just as she was about to head out the door, she heard a loud crash. Lizzy had forgotten her trick! She sprinted back over to the spot and saw that the plate had shattered and the egg was now all over the floor.

In her haste, the wild trick she had been so excited to perform had become a bad ending. All Lizzy could do was clean up the mess, she had lost her chance at the circus.

When they reached the park, Grandma's cane broke! She was so sad. She looked at Grandpa and asked, "What can I do now?"

Grandpa thought for a moment. He had an idea and said, "I will look for another cane." So Grandpa and Grandma looked around the park, but they couldn't find a new cane.

All of a sudden, Grandma started to feel tired. Her breathing became slow and heavy, and she became unable to move. Grandpa was scared and quickly called an ambulance.

The ambulance took Grandma to the hospital, but it was too late. Grandma had become too sick. She never made it out of the hospital. Grandpa was very sad. He wished he had found a new cane faster.

Once upon a time there was a child who had a useful toy. It was a toy that could carry things. The child was very excited and played with the toy all day long. 

One day, the child's mom asked them to carry the box of cookies to their grandparents' house. The child grabbed their toy and put the box on it. 

The child was worried that the cookies might topple over as they traveled, so they asked their mom, "Can I tie a rope around the box to make sure it doesn't fall off?" 

"No, it won't be necessary," the mom replied. 

However, the child was smart and decided to use the rope anyway. As the child walked up the hill, the rope kept the box securely in place.

Once upon a time, in the big and beautiful woods, there was a little bunny. It hopped around happily, enjoying the sunshine and the fresh air.

Suddenly, the bunny heard a loud noise coming from the nearby bushes. It hopped closer and peeked inside.

To the bunny's surprise, there was a big bear curled up inside. "Please don't be scared," said the bear. "I'm counting to ten before I come out."

The bunny was amazed! "What are you counting?" it asked.

"I'm counting to make sure it's safe," said the bear. "See, some places can be dangerous, and counting helps me decide when it's safe to come out."

The bunny thought carefully and smiled. "My mouth can help too," it said. "If it's safe, I'll open my mouth wide and I won't have to count."

The bear chuckled. "That's great, little one," said the bear. "But until we make sure it's safe, it's best to count!" 

And so the bear counted cautiously before it emerged. The bunny was glad to see that the woods were safe, and that it had a new friend too!

So, Tim cleaned his room. It was not fun, but he did it. After that, he was allowed to play with his pillow and rock again. Tim was very happy. He learned that sometimes he had to do things he didn't like, but it was worth it in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a big cloud in the sky. The cloud was very dry and wanted to find some water to make rain. The cloud floated high above the trees, looking for water.

One day, the cloud saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was playing outside and looked up at the cloud. She said, "Hello, cloud! Why are you so dry?" The cloud listened and said, "I need water to make rain, but I can't find any."

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I know where to find water! Follow me!" The cloud listened and followed Lily to a big lake. The cloud drank the water from the lake and became full of rain. Then, the cloud rained on the flowers and trees, making them very happy. Lily and the cloud became good friends and played together every day.

Just then, Tim's mom came into the room. She saw the napkin on Bob's head and laughed. "What a funny hat, Tim! Let's reveal a surprise for Bob!" Tim's mom took out a big box from the closet. She opened the box and took out a new toy bear.

"This is Daisy," said Tim's mom. "She can be Bob's friend!" Tim looked at Daisy and then at Bob. Bob was not moving. He looked dead. Tim was scared. "Mom, is Bob dead?" he asked.

Tim's mom smiled and said, "No, Tim. Bob is just a toy bear. He cannot be dead. He is just not moving because he is a toy." Tim felt better. He played with Bob and Daisy all day. And from that day on, the three friends were always together.

Lila and Ben nod. They are very sorry. They promise the guard.

"Let's go home," Ben says.

As they were walking, Lily saw a big puddle in front of her. She wanted to step in it but her mom said, "No, Lily. Your shoes will get wet." 

Lily felt sad but she listened to her mom. They kept walking and talking about all the things they saw. Lily was happy because she was spending time with her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his ball, which he would roll around the yard. One day, Timmy found a mysterious bottle in the grass. He picked it up and looked inside, but he couldn't see anything.

Timmy decided to take the mysterious bottle to his mom. She looked at it and told him to be careful because it might be dangerous. Timmy was scared, but he still wanted to know what was inside. He decided to roll the bottle around to see if anything would happen.

Suddenly, the mysterious bottle started to shake and smoke came out of it. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, the smoke cleared and a genie appeared! The genie granted Timmy three wishes and Timmy was very happy. He wished for a new bike, a puppy and a big ice cream cone. From that day on, Timmy always remembered to be careful when he found mysterious things and to never give up on his dreams.

Her mom replied, "The cars and trucks make noise when they move. It's just a regular sound we hear when we are outside."

Lucy and her mom kept walking. They saw a dog barking at the traffic. Lucy laughed and said, "The dog doesn't like the noise too!"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, some animals don't like loud sounds. But they get used to it, just like we do."

After their walk, Lucy and her mom went home. Lucy was happy that she learned something new about traffic and the noises it makes. She knew that it was just a regular part of being outside, and she wasn't scared of it anymore.

But then, it was time for Bunny to go home. Daisy started to complain. She said, "Bunny, I don't want you to go. I want to play more." Bunny said, "Don't be sad, Daisy. We can play again tomorrow." Daisy smiled and said, "Okay, Bunny. I will see you tomorrow." They hugged and Bunny went home. Daisy felt happy knowing she would play with her friend again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit. The rabbit had a difficult job. It had to cut the grass in the garden. The rabbit tried very hard to cut the grass, but it was not easy.

One day, a bird came to the rabbit and said, "Hello, rabbit! I see you have a difficult job. Can I help you cut the grass?" The rabbit was happy and said, "Yes, please! That would be nice!"

The bird and the rabbit worked together to cut the grass. They talked and laughed as they worked. Soon, the grass was all cut and the garden looked nice. The rabbit was very happy and thanked the bird for helping. From that day on, they were the best of friends.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big book full of wonder. He did not understand the words in the book. He felt embarrassed because he wanted to read the book to his friends.

Tim went to his friend, Sam, and said, "I found a book full of wonder, but I don't understand the words. Can you help me?" Sam looked at the book and said, "I don't understand the words either, but let's try to read it together."

They tried to read the book, but they still did not understand the words. They felt very sad. They left the book on the ground and went to play. Later, a big wind came and blew the book away. Tim and Sam never saw the book again.

The moral of the story is that if you don't understand something, ask for help from someone who knows more than you.

Once upon a time, in a big park, there was a little purple bird named Pip. Pip loved to play with his friends. One day, while playing, Pip found a small pebble. He thought it was very pretty and wanted to show his friends.

Pip went to his friend, the wise old owl. "Look what I found," Pip said. The wise old owl looked at the pebble and said, "This is a special pebble. You must keep it safe. One day, you will need it."

Pip did not understand, but he kept the pebble safe. Time went by, and one day, a big storm came. All the birds were scared and hid in their nests. The wind blew and blew, and Pip's nest was destroyed. Pip was very sad.

Then, Pip remembered the wise old owl's words. He took out the special pebble and held it tight. He ordered the wind to stop, and to his surprise, the wind stopped. Pip's friends came out and cheered. They all helped Pip build a new nest, and they lived happily ever after.

The next day, Lily's best friend came over to play. They were having fun until Lily's friend accidentally broke one of her toys. Lily got very upset and wanted to refuse to play with her friend anymore. But then, Lily remembered how she had refused to step on the scale and change her wet clothes. She realized that sometimes it's important to do things we don't want to do, and that it's not nice to refuse to play with our friends just because they made a mistake.

From that day on, Lily learned to be more understanding and kind to her friends, and to listen to her mom when she asked her to do something.

Timmy decided to lean the sandwich against his plate and not eat it. As he played with his toys, he heard a noise. It was his dog, Max. Max saw the sandwich and began to eat it. Timmy was happy that Max liked the sandwich, even though he did not. 

From that day on, Timmy's mom made him normal sandwiches with just ham and cheese. Timmy was happy and never had to lean his sandwich again. The end.

Timmy was sad because he wanted to catch a fish. His dad told him not to worry and that they would solve the problem. They decided to move to a different spot on the lake. Timmy cast his rod again and waited. This time, he felt a big tug on his line. He started to reel it in but it was too heavy. He asked his dad for help. They both pulled and pulled until they finally saw what was on the end of the line.

The end.

Sue and Tim talked about what went wrong. They decided to try again. This time, Sue showed Tim how to measure the right way. The cake was perfect. They learned that working together and teaching each other is the best way to solve a problem.

One day, a little girl named Lily wanted to watch a video on her mom's phone. She asked her mom, "Mom, can I watch a video, please?" Her mom said, "Yes, Lily, but only one video, then it's time to go outside and play."

Lily watched a video about a funny cat. The cat was playing with a ball and sometimes it would fall down. Lily laughed and laughed. But then, she saw another video about a dog and wanted to watch it too. She knew her mom said only one video, but she clicked on the dog video anyway.

After watching the dog video, Lily felt ashamed. She knew she should have listened to her mom. She went to her mom and said, "Mom, I watched two videos. I'm sorry." Her mom hugged her and said, "Thank you for telling me, Lily. Now, please close the phone and let's go play outside."

Lily closed the phone and went outside with her mom. They played with a ball, just like the cat in the video. Lily learned that it is important to listen to her mom and not to do things that make her feel ashamed.

"Spot! Spot!" Lily and Ben shouted. They wanted to help Spot, but they did not know how to swim. They looked around and saw a man with a boat. He had a jacket and a hat.

"Thank you! Thank you!" Lily and Ben said to the man. They hugged Spot and rubbed his fur. Spot licked their faces and wagged his tail.
