Lily and Sam went to the beach with their mom and dad. They wanted to play in the sand and swim in the water. But mom and dad said they had to observe the tide first. They said the tide was the water that goes up and down on the beach. Sometimes it is high and sometimes it is low.

Lily and Sam did not understand why they had to observe the tide. They thought it was boring. They wanted to have fun. They asked mom and dad, "Can we go now? Can we go now?"

Mom and dad said, "Not yet. We have to wait a little longer. The tide is low now. That means the water is far away from the beach. If we go now, we might get stuck in the mud or step on something sharp. We have to wait until the tide is high. That means the water is close to the beach. Then we can swim and play safely."

Lily and Sam sighed. They did not like to wait. They looked at the water and the sand. They saw some birds and some shells. They saw some boats and some fish. They saw some clouds and some sun. They started to observe the tide. They noticed that the water was moving slowly. It was coming closer and closer to the beach. They saw the sand getting wet and the shells getting covered. They saw the birds flying away and the fish jumping. They saw the boats rocking and the sun shining. They realized that the tide was not boring. It was interesting. It was changing.

They smiled at mom and dad. They said, "We observed the tide. We learned something new. The tide is high now. Can we go now? Can we go now?"

Mom and dad nodded. They said, "Yes, you can go now. You did a good job. The tide is high now. You can swim and play safely. But remember to stay close to us and watch out for the waves. The tide can also be strong and fast. It can push you and pull you. It can surprise you and scare you. The tide is interesting, but it is also powerful. You have to respect it and be careful."

Lily and Sam agreed. They said, "OK, we will. We will respect the tide and be careful. But we will also have fun. We love the tide. We love the beach. We love you."

They ran to the water and splashed and laughed. They had fun. They observed the tide. They learned something new.

"Hi, seal," Sara said. She reached out her hand to touch it.

But the seal did not want to play. It was scared and angry. It opened its mouth and showed its sharp teeth. It snapped at Sara's hand and bit it hard.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sara cried. She pulled back her hand and saw blood. It hurt a lot.

Mom and Dad heard her cry and ran to her. They saw the seal and the blood and were very worried.

"I wanted to touch the seal, but it bit me," Sara said, sobbing.

She hugged Sara and took her away from the seal. Dad followed them, shaking his head.

The seal swam away, feeling sorry for Sara, but also glad that she left him alone. He did not like to be touched by strangers. He liked to be with his friends and family. He hoped Sara would be okay, and that she would learn to respect animals.

One day, Ben and Lily went to visit their elderly grandma. She lived in a small house with a big garden. She liked to grow flowers and vegetables in her garden. She also had a cat named Patch, who had a black spot on his white fur.

"Hello, my dears!" Grandma said, hugging them. "I'm so happy to see you. Do you want to help me in the garden?"

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said. They liked to help Grandma and learn from her. She gave them each a small basket and a pair of gloves. "Today, we are going to pick some carrots and peas. Can you guess where they are?"

Ben and Lily looked around the garden. They saw roses, sunflowers, daisies, and tulips. They saw tomatoes, lettuce, cabbage, and corn. But they did not see any carrots or peas.

"Are they under the ground?" Ben asked.

"Very good, Ben!" Grandma said. "Carrots grow under the ground. You have to dig them up with a spade. But be careful not to hurt them. And peas grow on vines. You have to snap them off with your fingers. But be gentle not to break them. Do you want to try?"

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said. They followed Grandma to the carrot and pea patches. They put on their gloves and started to dig and snap. They had fun finding the carrots and peas and putting them in their baskets. They also found some worms and snails and showed them to Grandma.

"Look, Grandma, we found some friends!" Lily said.

"Wow, they are very interesting!" Grandma said. "But we have to put them back in the soil. They help the plants grow. And we have to wash our hands before we eat. Do you know who else likes to eat carrots and peas?"

"Who, Grandma?" Ben and Lily asked.

"Patch, of course!" Grandma said. "He is a very hungry cat. He likes to sneak into the garden and nibble on the vegetables. Sometimes he even digs up the carrots. That's why I have to put a fence around the patches. But he is also very sweet and cuddly. Do you want to see him?"

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily said. They followed Grandma to the house. They saw Patch sleeping on the couch. He opened his eyes and saw them. He jumped off the couch and ran to them. He rubbed his head against their legs and purred. He licked their hands and faces.

"Hello, Patch!" Ben and Lily said. They petted him and hugged him. "You are a very nice cat. But you are also a very naughty cat. You should not eat Grandma's vegetables. They are for us and for her. Do you understand?"

Patch looked at them with his big green eyes. He nodded his head and meowed. He seemed to understand. He was sorry for being naughty. He wanted to be a good cat.

"Good boy, Patch!" Grandma said. She smiled and kissed him. "You are forgiven. But you have to promise not to do it again. And you have to share with us. We have plenty of carrots and peas for everyone. Do you want some?"

Patch nodded his head and meowed. He wanted some. He was hungry. He followed Grandma to the kitchen. She washed the carrots and peas and cooked them. She made a delicious soup for them. She gave them each a bowl and a spoon. She also gave Patch a small plate with some carrots and peas. They sat around the table and ate. They thanked Grandma for the soup. They thanked Patch for being a good cat. They enjoyed their meal and their visit. They were happy.

"Where are you, Ben?" she called out. "I will find you!"

Ben was hiding in the kitchen. He had crawled into a big cupboard and closed the door. He was very quiet and still. He did not want Lily to find him. He wanted to win the game. He was very competitive.

Lily heard a noise in the kitchen. She ran there and looked around. She saw the fridge, the table, the chairs, and the cupboards. She opened one cupboard and saw some pots and pans. She opened another cupboard and saw some plates and cups. She opened the last cupboard and saw Ben.

"Got you!" she shouted. "You are the loser!"

Ben was surprised and sad. He did not like to lose. He wanted to keep hiding. He did not want to surrender.

"No, no, no!" he said. "Let me hide again! Please, Lily, please!"

Lily shook her head. She was happy and proud. She liked to win. She did not want to play again.

"No, no, no!" she said. "You are the loser! I am the winner! You have to surrender!"

"Ben was hiding in the cupboard and I found him and I said he is the loser and I am the winner and I did not want to play again and he said he wanted to hide again and he did not surrender and he did not listen to me and he was stubborn and silly and..." Lily said.

Lily and Ben agreed. They thanked their mom and ate their cookies. They decided to play a different game, but not hide and seek. They did not want to go to the cupboard again. They wanted to be nice and share and have fun.

One day, a bear and a bee were friends. The bear liked to eat honey, and the bee liked to make honey. The bee said to the bear, "I have a lot of honey in my home. Do you want some?"

The bear said, "Yes, please. I love honey. Can I go with you?"

The bee said, "Sure, but you have to be quiet and careful. My home is in a big tree, and there are many other bees there. They do not like strangers."

The bear and the bee went to the big tree. The bee showed the bear a hole in the trunk. The bee said, "This is where I live. The honey is inside. You can take some, but not too much. And do not touch anything else."

The bear nodded and followed the bee into the hole. He saw many jars of honey on the shelves. He picked one and opened it. He smelled the honey and licked his lips. He said, "This honey is very sweet and yummy. Thank you, bee."

The bee said, "You are welcome, bear. But hurry up. We have to go soon. The other bees will be back."

The bear said, "OK, OK. Just one more jar." He reached for another jar, but he did not see that it was not honey. It was something else. It was smelly and sticky. It was glue.

The bear touched the glue and got his paw stuck. He tried to pull it out, but he could not. He said, "Oh no! What is this? Help me, bee!"

The bee said, "Oh no! That is not honey. That is glue. The other bees use it to fix things. You should not have touched it. Now you are in trouble."

The bear said, "I am sorry, bee. I did not know. How can I get out?"

The bee said, "I do not know. Maybe we can find something to cut the glue. But we have to be fast. I hear the other bees coming. They will be angry if they see you here."

The bear and the bee looked around for something to cut the glue. They saw a knife on a table. The bee said, "There! That knife. Maybe we can use it."

The bear said, "Good idea, bee. But how can we get it? It is too far."

The bee said, "I have an idea. I will fly to the knife and bring it to you. You have to be brave and still."

The bear said, "OK, bee. I will try. But please hurry."

The bee flew to the knife and grabbed it with his legs. He flew back to the bear and said, "Here, bear. I have the knife. Hold still. I will cut the glue."

The bear said, "Thank you, bee. You are a good friend."

The bee said, "You are welcome, bear. You are a good friend, too. But we have to go now. The other bees are here. They are buzzing and stinging. They are not happy."

The bee cut the glue and freed the bear's paw. He said, "Come on, bear. Follow me. We have to get out of here."

The bear said, "OK, bee. Let's go." He grabbed the jar of honey and ran after the bee. They escaped from the hole and ran away from the big tree. They heard the other bees chasing them and shouting.

The bear and the bee ran until they were safe. They found a shady spot under a bush. They sat down and breathed hard. They looked at each other and smiled. They said, "That was a close call. But we made it."

The bee said, "Yes, we did. But next time, be more careful, bear. Do not touch things that are not honey."

The bear said, "I will, bee. I learned my lesson. But can I still have some honey?"

The bee said, "Of course, bear. You can have some honey. But only a little. And share it with me."

The bear said, "OK, bee. I will share it with you. You are my best friend."

The moral of the story is that it's important to be true to yourself and not do things just because someone else dares you to. It's also important to be kind to others and not pressure them into doing something they don't want to do.
